D096 — measured boot confirmed on RA8M2 by decoding the boot record; D095 had assumed it

Date: 2026-10-06 · Status: Accepted · Corrects: D095

D095 listed measured boot among the things RA8M2's regression run proved. It did not. D080 is explicit that a passing attestation suite cannot detect measured boot - with component_cnt == 0 the token carries IAT_NO_SW_COMPONENTS and the test still passes - which is why D081 verified RA6M5 by reading the record off the hardware. D095 made exactly the inference D080 exists to forbid. The PSA Arch attestation run (1/1, 16 checks) does not close it either, for the same reason.

Now actually verified. Boot record read from 0x22000000 (BOOT_TFM_SHARED_DATA_BASE = S_DATA_START = BSP_PARTITION_RAM_CPU0_S_START, 0x400 bytes) after the PSA Arch attestation run:

magic 0x2016, tot_len 195
TLV 0x107F, 92 B, IAS   NSPE  version 0.0.0  SHA256  168543c2…939df68d
TLV 0x103F, 91 B, IAS   SPE   version 2.2.0  SHA256  c0ce6eb9…6cb50842
                              + 32-byte signer ID and "SHA256" description on both

Both measurements equal the SHA-256 TLV (type 0x10) in the corresponding signed image, so BL2 hashed the real images rather than writing placeholders. Checked against m2cry/bin/tfm_s_signed.bin and m2att/bin/tfm_ns_signed.bin - the images that run actually boots, not the FLIH tree's.

The versions are incidental confirmation of DESIGN.md §1.1. SPE 2.2.0 / NSPE 0.0.0 are TF-M's MCUBOOT_IMAGE_VERSION_S and _NS, not FSP's MCUBOOT_IMAGE_VERSION environment variable. The documented deviation is visible in the boot record itself.

Method note. The first comparison used m2gflih's images out of habit and reported a mismatch on both. The dump came from the attestation launch, which boots m2cry/m2att. When a measurement does not match, check which image the board was actually running before concluding anything about the device.

D097 — RA8M2 PSA Arch: storage clean, crypto has one real failure — RSIP-E50D cannot generate RSA-2048 keys

Date: 2026-10-08 · Status: Accepted

Third and fourth RA8M2 PSA Arch suites run on hardware, GCC, profile_large / isolation 3 / IPC.

Storage: 11 pass / 0 fail / 6 skip — identical to RA6M5

Every skip is code 0x2b, "Optional PS APIs are not supported": tests 411, 412, 413, 415, 416, 417, all exercising psa_ps_create / psa_ps_set_extended, which TF-M does not implement. Test 414 explicitly checks that those calls fail and passes.

The result matters more than the number: PS and ITS here are backed by **DF_EMULATION, 64 KB of MRAM**, not real data flash. Test 403 "insufficient space" behaved correctly in both halves - ITS filled at UID 13, PS at UID 8, and both recovered after removing all UIDs. That is the first runtime evidence the DF_EMULATION split works as D086's corrected arithmetic predicted.

Crypto: TEST 216 FAILED, and it is a genuine capability gap

TEST: 216  psa_generate_key
  [Check 1] 16 Byte AES        ok
  [Check 2] 24 Byte AES        ok
  [Check 3] 32 Byte AES        ok
  [Check 4] RSA 2048 Keypair   Failed at Checkpoint 3, Actual -134, Expected 0

-134 is PSA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED. Only generation fails. RSA import (202), export (203), export_public (204), destroy (205), asymmetric encrypt (239), decrypt (240), sign_hash (241), verify_hash (242), verify_message (253) and copy_key (244) all pass with RSA-2048 keys.

RA6M5 does not have this gap. D046 recorded crypto 63 / 0 / 1 on SCE9, the single skip being deterministic ECDSA (D040). Test 216 passed there.

It is the engine, not the port

Checked, because an identical-looking config on two parts invites the assumption that one of them was mis-copied:

rm_psa_crypto tree, ra6m5_gcc_secure vs ra8m2_gcc_CPU0_securebyte-identical, every file
sce9_fsp_cfg.h vs rsip_e50d_fsp_cfg.hidentical apart from the include guard
RM_PSA_CRYPTO_CFG_RSA{3K,4K}_KEYGEN_ENABLED0 on both; no RSA-2K keygen flag exists either way

Same sources, same configuration, different silicon. **The RSIP-E50D does not implement RSA-2048 key generation and the SCE9 does.** MBEDTLS_RSA_ALT is defined, so the ALT replaces the whole RSA module and there is no software fallback to catch it.

Two things this raises

  1. The E50D accelerator config is a copy of the SCE9 one with the guard renamed. That was already noted as a restatement risk in D077. It is now demonstrably describing a part with different capabilities, which is the shape of defect that audit was looking for.
  2. Whether psa_generate_key for RSA should fall back to software. It currently returns NOT_SUPPORTED at run time rather than being refused at configuration time. An application that generates RSA keys on-device works on RA6M5 and fails on RA8M2, with nothing in the build to warn.

Not yet recorded

The RA8M2 crypto log was truncated before the suite summary, so the final pass/fail/skip tally is unknown. What is known: test 216 FAILED, test 252 (psa_sign_message) SKIPPED with code 0x2d, and every other test shown PASSED. RA6M5 had one skip; RA8M2 has at least one different one. The tail is worth capturing before this is reported as a final result.

D098 — refines D097: the RSA-2048 keygen failure is the PLAINTEXT path, and the config selects it

Date: 2026-10-08 · Status: Superseded by D111 · Corrects: D097 · Evidence: Corrects the reasoning in D097

D097 concluded "the RSIP-E50D does not implement RSA-2048 key generation". The observation was right and the reason was not. The precise position, from three independent sources:

1. The code

rm_psa_crypto/rsa_alt_process.c, the nbits == RSA_2048_BITS branch:

p_hw_sce_rsa_generatekey = g_rsa_keygen_lookup[(uint32_t) ctx->vendor_ctx];
if (true == (bool) ctx->vendor_ctx) {        /* WRAPPED key */
    private_key_size_bytes = sizeof(sce_rsa2048_private_key_index_t);
} else {                                     /* PLAINTEXT key */
#if !(BSP_FEATURE_RSIP_SCE7_SUPPORTED || BSP_FEATURE_RSIP_SCE9_SUPPORTED ||       BSP_FEATURE_RSIP_RSIP_E51A_SUPPORTED)
    ret = MBEDTLS_ERR_PLATFORM_FEATURE_UNSUPPORTED;
#endif

E50D is absent from that list, so only the plaintext path is refused. The wrapped path has no such guard.

2. rm_psa_crypto_usage_notes.md

RSAE50D
Key generation - plaintext--
Key generation - wrapped(3) = RSA-2048, 3072, 4096 only

So E50D generates RSA-2048 keys in wrapped format and not in plaintext.

3. The port asks for plaintext

/* rsip_e50d_fsp_cfg.h */
#define PSA_CRYPTO_CFG_RSA_FORMAT   (PSA_CRYPTO_CFG_PLAINTEXT_KEY_SUPPORT)

AES and ECC are set the same way. PSA therefore requests the one RSA keygen format this engine does not offer, and gets PSA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED at run time.

Why RA6M5 passes

BSP_FEATURE_RSIP_SCE9_SUPPORTED is in the guard list. Same sources, same config, different BSP_FEATURE_*. D097 was right that nothing in the port differs between the parts; it was wrong to infer from that that the capability was simply absent.

Also: RA8M2 is missing from the module's own device table

rm_psa_crypto_usage_notes.md lists RSIP-E50D → RA8P1. The BSP says otherwise:

partengine
ra6m5SCE9
ra8m2RSIP_E50D
ra8p1RSIP_E50D
ra8d1RSIP_E51A

RA8M2 is an E50D part and the table does not say so. Worth a line in the module docs - the table is what a reader consults to find out whether a part can do something, and reading it for RA8M2 today returns nothing.

What this does and does not change

Unchanged: PSA Arch crypto test 216 check 4 fails on RA8M2, and on-device RSA key generation in plaintext form is unavailable there while it works on RA6M5.

Changed: it is a key-format limitation, not a missing capability, and it is selected by a line in the port's own config. If wrapped RSA keys are acceptable to the application, PSA_CRYPTO_CFG_RSA_FORMAT is where to change it - with the caveat that switching formats affects import, export and storage of RSA keys as well, not just generation, so it is not a one-line fix to be made casually.

Method note

Two corrections from the user in two turns on this point, the second reversing the first. The authority was the module's own usage-notes table, in the same repository as the code. The lesson from D094 applies again: when the project documents the answer, read that before inferring one from behaviour.

D099 — closes D097's gap: RA8M2 crypto is 62/1/1, and the sole delta from RA6M5 is test 216

Date: 2026-10-08 · Status: Accepted · Builds on: D097 · Evidence: Completes the record left open by D097

The tally

************ Crypto Suite Report **********
TOTAL TESTS     : 64
TOTAL PASSED    : 62
TOTAL SIM ERROR : 0
TOTAL FAILED    : 1
TOTAL SKIPPED   : 1
RA6M5 (SCE9, D046)RA8M2 (RSIP-E50D)
passed6362
failed01 — test 216
skipped1 — test 2521 — test 252
total6464

The skip is the same skip on both parts

D097 said "RA6M5 had one skip; RA8M2 has at least one different one." Wrong. Both parts skip 252 (psa_sign_message), the deterministic-ECDSA gate from D040. Skip code 0x2d. There is no second skip and no new one.

So the two parts differ by exactly one test out of 64, and that test is the plaintext RSA-2048 keygen gap established in D098. Nothing else in the crypto suite distinguishes the RSIP-E50D from the SCE9 under this port.

What the full transcript adds beyond the tally

Three results in it are worth naming, because each could have been assumed to fail alongside 216 and does not:

  • 221 check 8, psa_key_derivation_output_key - RSA keypair: PASSED. Deriving an RSA keypair from a KDF is a different path from psa_generate_key and is not gated.
  • 244 checks 1-2, psa_copy_key with an RSA-2048 public key and keypair: PASSED.
  • 239/240 RSA PKCS1V15 and OAEP encrypt and decrypt, 241/242 sign_hash and verify_hash, 253 verify_message: all PASSED with RSA-2048.

Which sharpens D098: the plaintext guard in rsa_alt_process.c sits on generation alone. Every other plaintext RSA-2048 operation — import, export, copy, derive, encrypt, decrypt, sign, verify — works on the E50D.

  • 224/225 AEAD single-part GCM (check 9 on each) and 261/263 multi-part GCM finish and verify: PASSED. D041 recorded 261 and 263 failing on RA6M5 before two aes_alt.c fixes, and D045 then found 6.7.0-beta0 needs no port-local patches. Measured now: the 6.7 tree carries D041's fix 1 (mbedtls_aes_free() issues the matching FinalSub when state == UPDATE) and not fix 2 - mbedtls_aes_crypt_ctr() still opens with FSP_PARAMETER_NOT_USED(nc_off) and FSP_PARAMETER_NOT_USED(stream_block), drops the length % 16 tail in the unaligned path, and hands a partial length straight to the whole-block worker in the aligned path. aes_alt.c is byte-identical between ra6m5_gcc_secure and ra8m2_gcc_CPU0_secure (md5 f998be2b...), so this is 6.7 stock on both parts.

    So the GCM result confirms fix 1 holds on E50D silicon. It says nothing about fix 2, which is absent - and 236/237 pass anyway, including both "AES CTR (short input)" checks. The PSA cipher layer evidently never reaches mbedtls_aes_crypt_ctr() with a partial block or a live nc_off. That is a real coverage hole, not a resolved defect: the suite cannot see the bug D041 fixed, so a direct mbedtls_aes_crypt_ctr() caller on either part still hits it.

Status of the crypto result

Final and reportable. D097's "not yet recorded" section is closed; nothing in the tail changes D097 or D098's conclusions, and the one factual claim it corrects is the skip comparison above.

D100 — the MCUboot upgrade path runs on RA8M2: both images installed, secondary erased

Date: 2026-10-08 · Status: Accepted · Evidence: First execution of this path on any part in the port

ra8m2_TFM_update_gcc, GCC, on silicon. Primary slots flashed at 2.2.0, secondary slots at 2.3.0 by scripts/sign_secondary.py. Two consecutive boots:

[INF] Image index: 1, Swap type: test          [INF] Image index: 1, Swap type: none
[INF] Image 1 upgrade secondary slot -> primary slot
[INF] Erasing the primary slot
[INF] Image 1 copying the secondary slot to the primary slot
[INF] Image index: 0, Swap type: test          [INF] Image index: 0, Swap type: none
[INF] Image 0 upgrade secondary slot -> primary slot
[INF] Erasing the primary slot
[INF] Image 0 copying the secondary slot to the primary slot

Both images, not just the secure one - MCUBOOT_IMAGE_NUMBER=2 with OVERWRITE_ONLY and MCUBOOT_HW_ROLLBACK_PROT=ON. The second boot's Swap type: none is the other half of the proof: under OVERWRITE_ONLY the secondary is erased once installed, so a reset must not re-install, and it does not. The NS suites then ran to completion and passed.

Independently confirmed from the debugger before the BL2 log was recovered: rsp.br_hdr.ih_ver = 2.3.0 at rsp.br_image_off = 0x68000, with ih_magic 0x96f3b83d (IMAGE_MAGIC) and br_flash_dev_id 0x64 (FLASH_DEVICE_ID 100).

The slots are in REVERSE order on this part, and that is not a mistake

This is the detail that makes every address here read wrongly at first glance:

addressoffset
__BL_0_S_H_START - secure secondary0x020200000x20000
__BL_0_P_H_START - secure primary0x020680000x68000
__BL_1_P_H_START - NS primary0x120B0000
__BL_1_S_H_START - NS secondary0x120D8000

Image 0's secondary sits below its primary; image 1's does not. So br_image_off = 0x68000 is the primary slot, not the secondary, and a reader who assumes primary-then-secondary concludes BL2 booted the wrong slot. The ordering comes from the rzone partition layout, not from anything the port chooses. The four ra8m2_TFM_update_gcc flash rows were verified against ra8m2_gcc_CPU0_secure/Debug/bsp_linker_info.h one by one.

BL2's RTT output is unrecoverable after the chainload

region_defs.h:225 sets BL2_DATA_START to BSP_PARTITION_RAM_CPU0_S_START with BL2_DATA_SIZE = S_DATA_SIZE - BL2 and the SPE occupy the same RAM. The SPE's .bss zeroing wipes BL2's RTT control block microseconds after the jump, so a viewer that auto-detects after reset finds the SPE's block every time and BL2's banner is simply gone. This is why the first attempt showed nothing on the BL2 channel while the NS transcript was complete.

Control blocks for this build (nm <img> | grep ' _SEGGER_RTT$'; they move on every rebuild, D070):

image_SEGGER_RTT
bl2.axf0x22003cc8
tfm_s.axf0x2200ada0
tfm_ns.axf0x320ed4c8

To capture BL2: halt in BL2 (RA8M2_BL2_HALT_AT_MAIN=ON, or a breakpoint), point the viewer at BL2's address while halted, then run.

Two cosmetic log defects, neither worth patching

1. The byte count never prints. The line reads copying the secondary slot to the primary slot: 0xzx bytes. mcuboot/boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:1419 uses 0x%zx; BL2 links newlib-nano's integer-only formatter (printf aliases iprintf, _printf_i), which recognises the z length modifier only under _WANT_IO_C99_FORMATS - not defined in the nano variant. The % is consumed and zx prints literally. This is upstream MCUboot code and affects every platform linking nano printf. Not patched: the one number lost is recoverable from the image header, and diverging from upstream MCUboot for a log string is exactly what D091 went to trouble to avoid. Worth an upstream note, not a local fix.

2. "Swap type: test", not "perm". The build signs with --pad --pad-header ... --overwrite-only and no --confirm, so the trailer carries the magic but image_ok is unset and boot_swap_type() reports TEST. Under OVERWRITE_ONLY the distinction has no effect - there is no revert path and the secondary is erased - which the second boot confirms. Misleading to read, harmless in behaviour. sign_secondary.py inherits the flags from build.ninja verbatim, so adding --confirm would mean diverging from what the build actually does.

What this closes and what it does not

Closes: the MCUboot secondary-slot install path, previously never executed on either part. Does not close FWU - the PSA Firmware Update partition is still OFF (TFM_PARTITION_FIRMWARE_UPDATE), and TEST_S_FWU / TEST_NS_FWU have still never run. What is proven here is the bootloader half: BL2 correctly installs an image someone else placed in the secondary slot. Who places it there is the part FWU covers.

D103 — supersedes D102 on the IAR launch host project: it is the IAR project, and auto-config is false

Date: 2026-10-08 · Status: Accepted · Supersedes: D102 · Evidence: Corrects two attribute choices in D102

D102 generated the five RA8M2 IAR launches by copying the GCC twins and swapping build-tree paths only, on the evidence that the RA6M5 GCC/IAR pair differs in exactly nine lines, all paths. That evidence was sound and the conclusion drawn from it was still wrong in two places, both found by the rm_psa_crypto owner editing the launches by hand.

attributeD102 generatedcorrect
PROJECT_ATTRra8m2_gcc_CPU0_nonsecurera8m2_iar_CPU0_nonsecure
PROJECT_BUILD_CONFIG_AUTO_ATTRtruefalse
MAPPED_RESOURCE_PATHS entry/ra8m2_gcc_CPU0_nonsecure/ra8m2_iar_CPU0_nonsecure

Why the host project matters, having said it was incidental. serverParam builds the J-Link settings path from ${ProjName}:

-uJLinkSetting= "${workspace_loc:/${ProjName}}/${LaunchConfigName}.jlink"

With both toolchains hosted by one project, both write their .jlink sidecars into the same directory. Giving each toolchain its own host separates them. Nothing is built either way - ATTR_BUILD_BEFORE_LAUNCH_ATTR is 2, disabled - which is what made "incidental" look true.

auto=false was verifiable and was not checked. All six RA6M5 IAR launches that have run on hardware use PROJECT_BUILD_CONFIG_AUTO_ATTR=false; the GCC launches use true. The nine-line diff that justified copy-and-swap was taken from a GCC/IAR pair on the same part, where both already read false - so the attribute never appeared in the diff and the question never came up. **A diff between two correct files cannot show which fields are toolchain-dependent when both happen to agree.** The copy source here was an RA8M2 GCC launch, a different population.

What was done

ra8m2_TFM_flih_iar.launch had been missed by the hand edit - four of five changed - and was brought into line; the edit is byte-identical to the one applied to test_crypto. mk_iar_launches.py now performs the three substitutions, asserts each matches exactly once, and refuses to write a launch that still names the GCC project. --check reports **same for all five**, so the generator now reproduces the corrected files rather than reverting them - which is the property that makes a hand edit survivable.

Re-audited after the change, all five: setTZBoundaries false in both namespaces, ueraseRomOnDownload and ueraseDataRomOnDownload both 1, bl2.elf not bl2.bin, no GCC build tree referenced, all flash addresses among the four expected, MAPPED_RESOURCE_PATHS consistent with PROJECT_ATTR, and all 27 referenced files present.

ih_img_size is identical under both toolchains, and that is correct

Worth recording because it looks like a mis-flash. The watch shows 0x47a40 on IAR, exactly what the GCC run showed - yet IAR's tfm_s text is 2,126 B smaller (D102). Both images on disk really do carry 0x47a40, so it is not a stale binary. The reason is the layout:

secure payload starts      0x02068200
NSC veneer region starts   0x020AFC00   (fixed address)
payload 0x47a40 ends at    0x020AFC40
-> 0x47A00 of code region + 0x40 of veneers = 0x47A40

The image runs to the NSC veneers, which sit at a fixed address, so ih_img_size is set by the memory map rather than by how much code the compiler emitted. The text difference is slack inside the region. Expect this field to match across toolchains and to change only when the partition layout changes.

D107 — BL2 is silent under IAR because DLIB buffers stdout; rtt_stdout.c now makes it unbuffered

Date: 2026-10-09 · Status: Superseded by D108 · Evidence: Affects both parts; explains a symptom that looked like a wrong RTT address

The symptom and what it was not

BL2 produced no RTT output under IAR on RA8M2 while the secure and non-secure images printed normally. The obvious reading - stale or wrong control-block address - was wrong. Measured first, which is what settled it:

checkresult
_SEGGER_RTT from nm bl2.axf, bl2.map, nm bl2.elfall three agree, 0x22002d6c
MCUBOOT_LOG_LEVEL in the treeINFO
log strings in bl2.bin (Starting bootloader, Erasing the primary slot)present
__write provider in bl2.maprtt_stdout.o - the same object the printing tfm_s uses

Then the control block itself, dumped from the halted target:

acID              'SEGGER RTT'          <- initialised, so stdio_init() ran
MaxNumUpBuffers   3     MaxNumDownBuffers 3
aUp[0].pBuffer    0x22002E14   SizeOfBuffer 4096
aUp[0].WrOff      0                     <- BL2 wrote NOTHING
aUp[0].RdOff      0     Flags 0

A correctly formed block with WrOff == 0 is the whole diagnosis: SEGGER_RTT_Init() ran and __write() was never called. Nothing to do with the viewer or the address.

Cause

MCUboot's BOOT_LOG_* expand to printf(). IAR's DLIB buffers stdout and only calls __write() when the FILE buffer fills or something flushes it. BL2 logs a few hundred bytes and then chainloads - it never fills a buffer, never calls fflush, never exits. The text died in the C library.

The secure image hid it completely. TF-M's SPM logging calls stdio_output_string() directly and never goes through printf, so it was unaffected. That asymmetry is what made the symptom look BL2-specific and therefore like an address problem.

newlib line-buffers stdout, so GCC was never affected - which is why this survived a full GCC bring-up plus D104-D106's IAR runs.

Fix

setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0) in stdio_init(), guarded to __ICCARM__, in ra8m2/rtt/rtt_stdout.c and ra6m5/rtt/rtt_stdout.c. RA6M5 carries the same backend and the same latent defect; its IAR BL2 would also have been silent, unnoticed because the suite output comes from the other two images.

Verified: setvbuf now links into bl2.axf at 0x02004810.

The previous fix was right and incomplete

The same file already carried an IAR-specific __write(), added because DLIB calls __write and never _write, with a comment stating that was why BL2 produced no output under IAR. That diagnosis was correct and the hook was necessary - but getting a hook in place is not the same as output reaching it. Two independent defects on the same path, with the same symptom.

Scope

No test result changes. The images were correct and the suites genuinely ran; D104-D106 stand. What was broken is BL2's own logging under IAR, which is why D106's upgrade had to be confirmed from a boot_rsp watch rather than from the swap lines.

Cost, and the addresses move

tfm_s text276,468279,060 (+2,592, 14,316 B still free)
bl2 _SEGGER_RTT0x22002d6c0x22002d70
tfm_s _SEGGER_RTT0x2200aa640x2200ab64
tfm_ns _SEGGER_RTT0x320ed35c0x320ed45c

setvbuf pulls in stdio machinery both images had been linking without. Signed images are still exact slot fits and the secondaries have been re-signed.

D108 — supersedes D107's fix: the real hook is __dwrite, because TF-M redirects __write

Date: 2026-10-09 · Status: Accepted · Supersedes: D107 · Evidence: D107's diagnosis was half right and its fix made the symptom worse

What D107 got wrong

D107 found BL2's RTT control block correctly initialised with WrOff == 0, concluded DLIB stdout buffering was holding the text, and added setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0). The buffering is real and that call is still needed. It was not the reason __write never ran.

After the change BL2 did not print - it halted, and the call stack named the cause:

__iar_sh_stdout()          <- SEMIHOSTING
__dwrite()
__write_buffered()
fflushOne() / fputc() / putchar() / _Prout() / _PrintfFullNoMb()
printf()
tfm_plat_provisioning_perform()  provisioning.c:348

toolchain_IARARM.cmake:68-70:

add_link_options(
    --silent
    --semihosting
    --redirect __write=__write_buffered

Every reference to __write is redirected to DLIB's buffered writer. The port's __write in rtt_stdout.o was defined, present in nm and in the map, and unreachable - an orphan. The live path ran to __iar_sh_stdout from iarwstd.o.

So D107 converted a silent failure into a halt: with buffering, the text never flushed and semihosting was never reached; unbuffered, the first character hit the semihosting breakpoint and stopped the core. Correct direction, wrong mechanism, and worse in the interim.

Fix

Define __dwrite() as well. It is declared in IAR's <LowLevelIOInterface.h> with __write's exact signature:

__ATTRIBUTES size_t __dwrite(int, const unsigned char *, size_t);

Both hooks now share one implementation in <part>/rtt/rtt_stdout.c, on both parts: __write for builds without the redirect, __dwrite for builds with it - which TF-M always has. Defining it keeps dwrite.o and iarwstd.o out of the link entirely.

Verified on the rebuild:

beforeafter
__dwrite providerdwrite.o (library)rtt_stdout.o
__iar_sh_stdoutiarwstd.o, linkedabsent - semihosting not linked

Both fixes are needed; neither alone is sufficient. __dwrite gets the bytes to RTT instead of semihosting; setvbuf gets them out of the FILE buffer before BL2 chainloads.

Method note

Three wrong turns on one defect, each ruled out by measurement rather than argument: the RTT address (checked three ways, correct), the viewer (control block well formed), and buffering (D107, real but secondary). **The call stack settled in one look what four rounds of static checking could not** - the symbol tables showed __write present and said nothing about whether anything called it. Where a hook is defined but appears not to run, read the stack before reasoning about the build.

Upstream

Filed as item 14 in UPSTREAM_CHANGES.md. It is a report, not a carried diff: no upstream file is modified, so the 21-file count there is unchanged. The argument is that the two options are unconditional and together make it impossible for any IAR platform to supply its own low-level stdout - TF-M's own platform/ext/common/uart_stdout.c defines an IAR __write() that is equally dead under the stock toolchain file.

Cost and the addresses, again

tfm_s text279,060278,828
bl2 _SEGGER_RTT0x22002d700x22002d68
tfm_s _SEGGER_RTT0x2200ab640x2200ab64
tfm_ns _SEGGER_RTT0x320ed45c0x320ed45c

Slightly smaller than D107's build - the semihosting modules are gone. Secondaries re-signed.

D109 — the IAR BL2 log works; it closes D106's open item and refines D099's %zx finding

Date: 2026-10-09 · Status: Accepted · Builds on: D108 · Evidence: Confirms D108 on hardware

ra8m2_TFM_update_iar, BL2 RTT at 0x22002d68. The full log, first boot then second:

[INF] Image index: 1, Swap type: test            [INF] Image index: 1, Swap type: none
[INF] Image 1 upgrade secondary slot -> primary slot
[INF] Erasing the primary slot
[INF] Image 1 copying ...: 0x28000 bytes
[INF] Image index: 0, Swap type: test            [INF] Image index: 0, Swap type: none
[INF] Image 0 upgrade secondary slot -> primary slot
[INF] Erasing the primary slot
[INF] Image 0 copying ...: 0x48000 bytes
                                                 [INF] Bootloader chainload address offset: 0x68000
                                                 [INF] Image version: v2.3.0

D108 is confirmed on hardware. __dwrite reaches RTT, no semihosting, no halt.

Three things this closes

1. D106's open item. That entry recorded the IAR install but noted the erase half was not observed. The second boot reports Swap type: none for both images, so the secondary is erased once installed and a reset does not re-install. The IAR upgrade cycle is now evidenced end to end, as GCC's was in D100.

2. The chainload is stated outright, not inferred. chainload address offset: 0x68000 and Image version: v2.3.0 - BL2 naming the slot and the version it hands control to. D106 had to read this out of a boot_rsp watch because BL2 was silent. 0x02068000 - 0x02000000 = 0x68000 is __BL_0_P_H_START, the primary, confirming D100's reverse slot order from BL2's own mouth.

3. The copied byte counts check out against the slots:

loggedslot / signed image
Image 1 (NS)0x28000 = 163,840163,840
Image 0 (S)0x48000 = 294,912294,912

Whole-slot copies, which is what OVERWRITE_ONLY does.

D099's %zx finding was right about the cause and too broad about the scope

D099 recorded the GCC log printing 0xzx bytes and attributed it to mcuboot/.../loader.c using 0x%zx while BL2 links newlib-nano's integer-only formatter, which recognises the z length modifier only under _WANT_IO_C99_FORMATS. It then said this "affects every platform linking nano printf".

Under IAR the byte count prints correctly - 0x28000, 0x48000 above. IAR builds with --dlib_config=full (D102's toolchain flags), and full DLIB handles %z. So the defect is specific to the newlib-nano formatter, not to MCUboot's format string, and the decision not to patch upstream MCUboot stands on firmer ground than when it was made: the format string is valid C99 and the limitation is in the library a platform chooses to link.

Worth noting for anyone comparing transcripts: the same build under two toolchains will differ in this one line, and the GCC one is the degraded one.

Status

Every RA8M2 suite and the upgrade path now pass on both toolchains, with BL2's own log available under both. Nothing is outstanding against M5.

D110 — corrects the framing of D107/D108: the root cause is the call route, not the buffering

Date: 2026-10-09 · Status: Accepted · Corrects: D107, D108 · Evidence: Correction from the rm_psa_crypto owner

The owner's summary, which is the right one: *the issue was not that IAR buffered BL2's 400 bytes and failed to flush them - it was that BL2 printed by a different call than the secure image.* Both earlier entries led with buffering and buried that.

The two effects, separated

causeeffect
Output never reached RTTBL2 logs via printf -> DLIB -> __write redirected to __write_buffered -> __dwrite -> __iar_sh_stdout. The secure image calls stdio_output_string() directly and never enters DLIB.aUp[0].WrOff == 0
Symptom was silent rather than haltDLIB buffering - the bytes never flushed, so the semihosting trap was never reachedno halt, no diagnostic

What D107 got wrong specifically. Its comment said the buffering was why WrOff was 0 - "the text never left the C library". Wrong. WrOff was 0 because the output went to semihosting. A perfect flush would have produced the same WrOff == 0, which is exactly what D107's own build then demonstrated by halting instead of printing.

Buffering decided which failure you saw, not where the bytes went.

Both fixes are still required, and the evidence is three builds

Checked rather than assumed, because the obvious follow-on question is whether setvbuf is now redundant. It is not. Three builds differing only in these two changes:

setvbuf__dwriteresult
nonosilent, WrOff 0, no halt - the buffer holds it
yesnoHALT in __iar_sh_stdout - buffer released it, backend was semihosting
yesyesfull log on RTT

The middle row is the proof that buffering alone blocks delivery: releasing it changed the failure mode, so the bytes were genuinely stuck. Remove setvbuf today and BL2's output would sit in the FILE buffer and never reach __dwrite. No fourth build was needed - the three already run answer it.

Why this matters beyond the wording

The asymmetry is the generalisable part. Two logging routes exist in this codebase - stdio_output_string() direct, and printf through the C library - and only one of them was ever exercised by the images that print. Any future backend change must be tested against BL2, not just the secure image, or it will look correct while MCUboot's logging is dead. That is the lesson, not "IAR buffers stdout".

Comments in <part>/rtt/rtt_stdout.c corrected on both parts to lead with the route and to carry the three-build table.

D111 — supersedes D098: there is no config switch for the RSA-2048 keygen gap; the guard is on the engine

Date: 2026-10-09 · Status: Accepted · Corrects: D098, D099, D104 · Evidence: Corrects D098, and the wording it put into D099, D104 and the management milestone page

What D098 claimed, and why it was wrong

D098 concluded the plaintext RSA-2048 keygen failure was "a key-format limitation **selected by our own config**", named PSA_CRYPTO_CFG_RSA_FORMAT as "where to change it", and cited rsip_e50d_fsp_cfg.h as setting it to plaintext. Checked against the generated tree today:

claimreality
rsip_e50d_fsp_cfg.h sets the formatNo such file in ra8m2_gcc_CPU0_secure/ra/fsp/src/rm_psa_crypto/
our config selects plaintextra_cfg/arm/mbedtls/config.h:29 -> PSA_CRYPTO_CFG_RSA_FORMAT 3 = plaintext and wrapped
the RASC project asks for plaintextboth parts set config.driver.psa_crypto.rsa_format.vendor_plaintext_wrapped, which is also the RA8M2 BSP default

The actual mechanism

rsa_alt_process.c, in mbedtls_rsa_gen_key() at nbits == RSA_2048_BITS:

p_hw_sce_rsa_generatekey = g_rsa_keygen_lookup[(uint32_t) ctx->vendor_ctx];
if (true == (bool) ctx->vendor_ctx) {          /* WRAPPED - no guard */
    ...
} else {                                       /* PLAINTEXT */
#if !(BSP_FEATURE_RSIP_SCE7_SUPPORTED || BSP_FEATURE_RSIP_SCE9_SUPPORTED || \
      BSP_FEATURE_RSIP_RSIP_E51A_SUPPORTED)
    ret = MBEDTLS_ERR_PLATFORM_FEATURE_UNSUPPORTED;
#endif

The guard is entirely on BSP_FEATURE_RSIP_*_SUPPORTED - the silicon. E50D is not in that list, so plaintext RSA-2048 keygen is refused on RA8M2 and permitted on RA6M5 (SCE9). The format config does not appear in the guard at all; it only controls which entries of g_rsa_keygen_lookup[] are compiled, and with 3 both are.

PSA Arch test 216 calls psa_generate_key with default attributes, which is a plaintext key, so it takes the refused branch.

What this changes

  • There is no switch. D098's "if wrapped RSA keys are acceptable, PSA_CRYPTO_CFG_RSA_FORMAT is where to change it" is wrong: it is already 3, and raising it cannot help because the refusal is not conditioned on it. Getting hardware RSA keygen on E50D requires the caller to request a wrapped/vendor key (ctx->vendor_ctx true), which a conformance test neither does nor should.
  • The one-line summary becomes simpler and worse: RSIP-E50D has no plaintext RSA-2048 key generation primitive. Not a configuration choice - a capability the part lacks and SCE9 has. D097's original instinct was closer than D098's correction of it.
  • Management page corrected. It said "our configuration asks for the plain format... a known switch". Both halves were false and it was the only false statement on a page sent outside the team.

Method note

D098 was itself written to correct D097, after two user corrections in two turns, and it over-corrected: it reached for a config explanation and cited a file without opening it in the tree the result came from. **Three entries on one question, and the error that survived longest was the one written to fix an earlier error.** The check that would have caught it at any point is grep PSA_CRYPTO_CFG_RSA_FORMAT ra_cfg/arm/mbedtls/config.h on the project that produced the failing run - one command against generated output, rather than reasoning from module sources.

D112 — D101's parity method cannot read the azone; one regenerate produced different TrustZone assignments per toolchain

Date: 2026-10-12 · Status: Accepted · Builds on: D101 · Evidence: RA8M2, both toolchains

D101 declared the RA8M2 IAR and GCC projects configuration-identical on the strength of "a full <property id=... value=...> diff of all three pairs". That diff reads configuration.xml. Peripheral-to-zone assignments are not in that file - they live in .secure_azone / .secure_rzone, which the method never opened.

What the blind spot held, measured today:

Azone content, NS projectGCCIAR, before today
<peripheral name="AGT0.CPU0" group="AGT" security="s"/>presentpresent
<peripheral name="ICU.CPU0"><slot name="IRQ0.CPU0" secure="true"/>presentabsent
<assign group="AGT" peripheral="AGT0"/>presentpresent
<assign peripheral="ICU.IRQ0"/>presentabsent

The mechanism is the finding; the damage is nil

The ICU block is inert on both toolchains. Nothing in any RA8M2 project instantiates r_icu or external_irq - grepping all six configuration.xml files for either name returns nothing - so no driver claims IRQ0 and no vector entry is emitted for it. That is why IAR passed the full regression including the FLIH interrupt test (D105) without it: the FLIH fixture is AGT-based (D061, D101) and the AGT half was present on both sides all along.

Where it came from is what is worth keeping. 2b5015c ("Regenerate the RA6M5 and RA8M2 GCC/IAR projects with the secure AGT timer", 2026-10-01) touched all six RA6M5/RA8M2 azones in one step:

  • GCC NS tree: a 6-line addition - the AGT peripheral, the ICU block, and both assigns.
  • IAR NS tree: a 28-line rewrite (14+/14-) that did not include ICU.
  • git log -S'ICU' -- ra8m2_iar_CPU0_nonsecure/.secure_azone returns nothing. The IAR file never carried the block at any point.

One regeneration step, two different azones. RASC rewrote the IAR azone wholesale where it patched the GCC one, and the rewrite dropped a peripheral the patch added.

Consequence

  • The IAR azone is brought into line; the three lines are now identical across toolchains.
  • .secure_azone and .secure_rzone join the parity check. A property diff of configuration.xml is necessary and not sufficient: TrustZone peripheral security is decided in files it does not read. Any future "the projects agree" claim must diff the azones too.
  • D101's conclusion stands - the remaining differences really are inert - but it was reached by a method that could not have found a non-inert one. The claim was true by luck.

Rejected

Leave the IAR azone alone, since the block is inert. It is inert today, because no module claims IRQ0. The first module that does would make the two toolchains disagree on whether that interrupt is secure, and the symptom would surface in the NS image on one toolchain only - the most expensive shape of defect this port has had. Parity costs three lines.

Treat it as evidence that D101 was wrong. It is not. D101 fixed three real gaps and its parity finding holds; what this entry corrects is the sufficiency of the method, which matters for the next port (PORTING.md) rather than for RA8M2.

D113 — isolation 2 on silicon: TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL never reached the isolation HAL, and was hiding four port defects

Date: 2026-10-21 · Status: Accepted · Builds on: D061, D068, D101 · Evidence: RA6M5 measured, RA8M2 changed in step

The TF-M regression suite had never been run above isolation 1. Every tests_reg build in C:\b is L1/SFN and every L3 build is PSA Arch, which has no MMIO partitions and no IRQ suite. Running it at isolation 2 took five rounds, each fault hidden behind the previous.

**Result: RA6M5 at isolation 2, GNUARM — secure 9/9 suites PASSED, non-secure 7/7 PASSED, including TFM_NS_IRQ_TEST_FLIH_1101 and 1102.** First green regression run above isolation 1 on this port.

The MPU, measured rather than assumed

[MPU] regions in hardware: 8        <- read from MPU->TYPE; "8" had been an assumption
[MPU] enabled after static boundaries: 5
[MPU] CTRL: 7                        <- ENABLE | HFNMIENA | PRIVDEFENA
[MPU] --- after partition init ---   6 enabled
  idx 0  0x000A0400 - 0x000A5640     combined unprivileged/ARoT code
  idx 1  0x000A5660 - 0x000D82E0     PSA RoT code
  idx 2  0x000D8300 - 0x000E5BC0     RO data
  idx 3  0x20000400 - 0x200018A0     App RoT data
  idx 4  0x200018C0 - 0x20011480     PSA RoT data
  idx 5  0x400E8000 - 0x400E80E0     AGT0, from the FLIH service's mmio_region

Five static on a Cortex-M33 (PXN needs armv8.1-m.main, so the combined-code branch is taken), six with the peripheral bound. Two spare. RA8M2's count is still unread - its config.cmake claims "the RA8M2 Cortex-M33 has the 8-region MPU it assumes" and CPU0 is a Cortex-M85, so that sentence is inherited from RA6M5 and unverified.

The root cause is upstream, and silent

platform_s links tfm_config, not psa_interface - and psa_interface is the only target carrying TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL (interface/CMakeLists.txt:37). So platform/ext/common/tfm_hal_isolation_v8m.c, which switches on that macro throughout, compiles with it undefined on every platform using the shared HAL. #if on an undefined macro is 0, with no diagnostic.

What that silently produced at isolation 2:

Test in the HALWith the macro undefinedEffect
#if TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL == 1falseprivileged = IS_PSA_ROT() - ARoT partitions ARE de-privileged
#if TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL == 2falsethe named-MMIO region is never programmed
#if TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL != 3trueApp RoT data region present (consistent with idx 3)

Isolation enforced, the peripheral grant that makes it usable dropped. Confirmed by reading the compile line (-DCONFIG_TFM_ENABLE_MEMORY_PROTECT present, no -DTFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL) and by the region count going 5 -> 6 the moment the define was added.

Fixed port-locally with target_compile_definitions(platform_s PRIVATE ...) rather than in platform/CMakeLists.txt, to keep the shared-file delta small. Logged for upstream.

The four port defects it was masking

Each was real, each only reachable once the partitions were genuinely unprivileged, and each was found by the fault moving to the next one:

#FaultWhereFix
1MMFSR 0x01 IACCVIOL, PC 0x000BA964plat_test.c in platform_s -> PT_PSA_ROT_CODE, privileged-execute onlymove the file to tfm_sprt
2MMFSR 0x82, MMFAR 0x20011493static bool plat_test_timer_opened -> PT_PSA_ROT_DATA. tfm_sprt's code is unprivileged but its .bss is notdelete the static; SPRT must be stateless
3MMFSR 0x82, MMFAR 0x400E8008the AGT0 write itself - no MMIO region existed (the root cause above)define TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL
4MMFSR 0x82, MMFAR 0x40006300ICU IELSR cleared from the FLIH handlermove the ICU/NVIC clear into the vector entry

Two things that were asserted and turned out to be false

FSP's driver API cannot be called from an unprivileged partition. R_AGT_Open() calls R_BSP_IrqCfgEnable(), which writes the NVIC - PPB, privileged-only by architecture, so no MPU region can grant it. That is FSP-wide, not an AGT quirk: r_spi has 12 such call sites, r_iic_master 7, r_sci_uart 5, r_canfd 5. And g_timer0_ctrl lives in ra_gen/ at 0x2000fd54, inside PT_PSA_ROT_DATA. So the open moved to tfm_timer0_irq_init() (privileged, SPM-called) and start/stop became bare AGTCR writes. Note R_AGT_Open() re-enables the NVIC IRQ, undoing FF-M's "arrives disabled" guarantee - the disable is re-applied after it.

TF-M runs FLIH handlers in THREAD mode at the partition's privilege, not Handler mode. This was asserted in a code comment and used to justify leaving the NVIC clear in clear_intr(). The dump says otherwise: "came from secure FW in thread mode", faulting on the ICU write. The port's own vector entry TFM_TIMER0_IRQ_Handler() is Handler mode, so the controller-level clears live there and the partition's handler clears only AGT0's TUNDF, which its mmio_region covers.

Isolation costs what the backend costs, not what the level costs

Measured across four builds, both parts, GNUARM MinSizeRel, regression + FLIH:

StepRA6M5 textRA6M5 bssRA8M2 textRA8M2 bss
SFN -> IPC backend+4,606+13,092+6,337+13,720
isolation 1 -> 2+1,524+8+1,526+8
isolation 2 -> 3+1560+1560

The entire isolation machinery, L1 to L3, is ~1,680 B of text and 8 B of bss. Everything else is the IPC backend, which isolation 2 forces (set_config.cmake:35 turns on CONFIG_TFM_SPM_BACKEND_IPC for any level above 1 whatever string is passed - L2+SFN is an incoherent pair that surfaces as the manifest tool rejecting TFM_SP_IPC_{SERVICE,CLIENT}_TEST). Isolation 3 is essentially free; the step that costs anything is the one from L1.

Method note

Four rounds were spent moving a fault forward one layer at a time while reasoning from source that had not been confirmed reachable. The manifest, the allow-list, the platform_data_t bounds and the alignment checks were all verified correct before anyone asked whether the code that consumes them was compiled in. The instrument that settled it - tfm_hal_post_partition_init_hook() dumping every enabled region - was identified two rounds before it was used. Read the compile line before trusting the source.

Carried

  • RA8M2 at isolation 2 and 3, and all four IAR trees, rebuilt with these fixes but not yet run.
  • L1 + IPC still HardFaults on the PendSV write in arch_attempt_schedule (backend_ipc.c:517), precise BusFault, BFAR 0xE000ED04. Possibly the same root cause - with the macro undefined, privileged = IS_PSA_ROT() applies at isolation 1 too, where upstream intends true - but that does not yet explain why it failed earlier in boot than L2 did. Needs its own rebuild and run. L1+IPC is not a configuration this port ships.
  • ADDING_FSP_MODULES.md §7 documents the general pattern for using an FSP driver from a partition, including the PSA-RoT escape hatch, which is the answer for most users.

D114 — isolation 3 green too; the missing macro was not one macro, it is that platform_s never links psa_interface

Date: 2026-10-21 · Status: Accepted · Builds on: D113 · Evidence: RA6M5 measured

D113 was written after the isolation-2 run and attributed the whole chain to one absent compile definition, TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL. The isolation-3 run found a second one immediately, which reframes the finding: the problem is not a macro, it is that platform_s does not link psa_interface at all, so the shared isolation HAL silently loses every definition that interface carries.

**Result: RA6M5 at isolation 3, GNUARM — secure 9/9, non-secure 7/7, both FLIH tests PASSED.** With D113's isolation-2 run, the regression suite is now green at L1, L2 and L3 on this part.

The second macro, and why only level 3 exposed it

The L3 static table is an if/elif with no else:

#if   TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL != 3               /* -> App RoT data region   */
#elif defined(CONFIG_TFM_PARTITION_META)     /* -> TFM_SP_META_PTR region */
#endif

CONFIG_TFM_PARTITION_META is another psa_interface INTERFACE definition. Undefined, neither arm fires: level 3 programmed FOUR static regions instead of five, and nothing covered the partition-metadata pointer the SPM dereferences.

[MPU] enabled after static boundaries: 4     <- the App RoT data region at 0x20000400 absent
MMFSR 0x82, MMFAR 0x20000400                 <- TFM_SP_META_PTR itself

After adding the define, 5 static regions with idx 3 base 0x20000400 limit 0x20000400 - a 32-byte region, which is what TFM_SP_META_PTR is (0x20000400-0x20000420); both registers read the same value because RLAR[31:5] masks the low bits.

Level 2 could not have caught this: there the != 3 arm wins and the App RoT data region appears regardless.

Expected region counts, now measured at both levels

L2L3
static55
after partition init6 - MMIO appended permanently at bind time5 - MMIO is programmed per context switch, so the post-partition hook cannot see it

L3 showing 5 is correct, not a regression. Absence in that dump proves nothing at L3.

A third instance, not fixed because this port does not use it

TFM_PXN_ENABLE is tested with #ifdef in the same file and is **never converted into a compile definition anywhere in TF-M** - it exists only as a CMake cache variable. The PXN arms of the static MPU table are therefore unreachable on every platform. Harmless at the default (PXN is OFF, and check_config.cmake:91 permits it only on armv8.1-m.main), but an RA8 build setting TFM_PXN_ENABLE=ON would silently get no PXN attributes and no warning.

The corrected upstream position

UPSTREAM_CHANGES.md item 15 should argue for linking psa_interface into platform_s rather than adding macros one at a time, because the macro-by-macro fix only finds the ones someone has already been bitten by. What the HAL depends on:

MacroReaches the HAL?
CONFIG_TFM_ENABLE_MEMORY_PROTECTyes - platform/CMakeLists.txt:125
CONFIG_TFM_MMIO_REGION_ENABLEyes - generated config_impl.h, via spm_load_api.h -> interrupt_defs.h -> psa/service.h
TFM_ISOLATION_LEVELno - psa_interface only (D113)
CONFIG_TFM_PARTITION_METAno - psa_interface only (this entry)
TFM_PXN_ENABLEno - nowhere in TF-M

Method note, continued from D113

D113's note said "read the compile line before trusting the source". The follow-up lesson is narrower and sharper: **when a missing definition is found, enumerate what else the same translation unit depends on rather than fixing the one that happened to bite.** One grep over the file's #if/#ifdef conditions would have found all three in the same pass and saved a build-and-run cycle.

Carried

  • RA8M2 at L2 and L3, and all four IAR trees, are rebuilt with both defines but not yet run. RA8M2's hardware MPU region count is still unread - see D113.
  • L1 + IPC still HardFaults in arch_attempt_schedule. The privileged = IS_PSA_ROT() mis-evaluation at level 1 is now a stronger hypothesis, since the same undefined macro caused it, but the control build predates every fix and has not been rerun.
  • CONFIG_TFM_POST_PARTITION_INIT_HOOK and the per-region dump are still enabled on both ports. They are what made D113 and this entry possible and cost nothing below isolation 2, but they are diagnostics and should be reviewed before the port is called done.

D115 — RA8M2's MPU measured at 8 regions; corrects D114 on PXN; the diagnostic hook itself broke L1+IPC

Date: 2026-10-21 · Status: Accepted · Corrects: D114 · Evidence: RA8M2 measured

Three findings, in descending order of how wrong the prior entry was.

1. RA8M2's region count, finally read off the silicon

D113 and D114 both carried "RA8M2's hardware MPU region count is still unread". It is 8.

[MPU] regions in hardware: 8          <- MPU->TYPE, Cortex-M85, isolation 2
[MPU] enabled after partition init: 6
  idx 0  0x02068400 - 0x0206D680      combined unprivileged/ARoT code
  idx 1  0x0206D6A0 - 0x020A4860      PSA RoT code
  idx 2  0x020A4880 - 0x020ADB40      RO data
  idx 3  0x22000400 - 0x220018A0      App RoT data
  idx 4  0x220018C0 - 0x2200FEC0      PSA RoT data
  idx 5  0x40221000 - 0x402210E0      AGT0 - this part's base, not RA6M5's 0x400E8000

Result: RA8M2 at isolation 2, GNUARM — secure 9/9, non-secure 7/7, both FLIH tests PASSED. At isolation 3 the static set is five with idx 3 0x22000400 - 0x22000400, the 32-byte TFM_SP_META_PTR region, so the CONFIG_TFM_PARTITION_META fix from D114 is confirmed on the M85 as well. The secure suite passed as far as the captured log runs; the isolation-3 non-secure half has not been read back yet.

ra8m2/config.cmake claimed "the RA8M2 Cortex-M33 has the 8-region ARMv8-M MPU it assumes". The number was right and the core name was wrong - CPU0 is a Cortex-M85 - so the sentence was two-thirds inherited from RA6M5 and happened to land on the correct count. Corrected in place, and tfm_hal_platform.c's "unverified until the first run prints it" block now records what the run printed.

Five static entries on the M85, same as the M33. That is the combined-code branch, which matters for the next item.

2. D114 was wrong about PXN

D114's macro table ends with TFM_PXN_ENABLE → "no - nowhere in TF-M", and asserts the PXN arms of the static table are "unreachable on every platform". That is false.

# platform/CMakeLists.txt, pristine upstream
target_compile_definitions(platform_s
    PUBLIC
        ...
125:    $<$<OR:$<VERSION_GREATER:${TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL},1>,...>:CONFIG_TFM_ENABLE_MEMORY_PROTECT>
126:    $<$<BOOL:${TFM_PXN_ENABLE}>:TFM_PXN_ENABLE>

It is emitted on the line immediately after the macro D113 correctly identified as reaching the HAL, in the same PUBLIC block, on the same target. PXN reaches tfm_hal_isolation_v8m.c and works; it is how corstone300/310, mps4 and rse get PXN attributes from set(TFM_PXN_ENABLE ON) in their own config.cmake.

The error was reading an absence off a compile line without asking why it was absent. TFM_PXN_ENABLE defaults OFF, so $<$<BOOL:OFF>:...> collapses to nothing and the define is genuinely missing from every compile line in C:\b. Missing because unset looks exactly like missing because unplumbed. TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL was the second kind; this was the first, and the same observation was used to reach both conclusions.

Consequence for this port: setting TFM_PXN_ENABLE=ON on RA8M2 would really split the combined-code region and really need a sixth static entry. With 8 in hardware that fits. It stays OFF - no measurement supports turning it on - but it is an available option rather than dead code, which is the opposite of what D114 recorded.

3. The diagnostic hook broke the one configuration it was never built in

D114's last line says the post-partition hook "cost[s] nothing below isolation 2". Rebuilding the L1+IPC controls - stale since before any of these fixes - produced:

secure_fw/spm/core/spm_ipc.c:440: undefined reference to `tfm_hal_post_partition_init_hook'

Two guards that have to agree and did not:

guard
call site, spm_ipc.c:435#if CONFIG_TFM_POST_PARTITION_INIT_HOOK == 1
body, tfm_hal_platform.c#ifdef CONFIG_TFM_ENABLE_MEMORY_PROTECT
enable, config_tfm_target.hunconditional

So the caller appears whenever the hook is enabled, but the body appears only above isolation

  1. Three of the four corners are safe and that is why it survived: L1+SFN has no call site at all (the hook is called only from spm_ipc.c, and the SFN backend is a different file); L2 and L3 define CONFIG_TFM_ENABLE_MEMORY_PROTECT and get both halves. Only L1 + IPC has the caller without the body - and L1+IPC is the one configuration this port does not ship and had not been rebuilt since the hook was added.

This one is ours, not upstream's. Five Arm platforms (rse/kronos, rd1ae, rdv3, rdv3r1, tc) also #define CONFIG_TFM_POST_PARTITION_INIT_HOOK 1 unconditionally, but their body in tfm_hal_isolation_rse.c has no #ifdef around it, so caller and body always agree. This port put the body inside the memory-protect guard - it had to, because it calls SPMLOG_* and the region-dump helpers that are themselves inside that guard - and then left the enable unconditional. Nothing to send upstream.

Fixed by gating the enable on the same macro the body is gated on, so the two track each other:

#ifdef CONFIG_TFM_ENABLE_MEMORY_PROTECT
#define CONFIG_TFM_POST_PARTITION_INIT_HOOK     1
#endif

Verified a no-op above isolation 1 by rebuilding m5gl2 on the patched source and comparing tfm_s.elf against the binary that produced the green isolation-2 run: byte-identical. So the eight L2/L3 trees already built, the four IAR ones included, are still exactly what this source produces and do not need rebuilding.

Safe because config_base.h:351 already supplies #ifndef → 0, so leaving it undefined is the sanctioned way to turn it off, and because CONFIG_TFM_ENABLE_MEMORY_PROTECT is PUBLIC on platform_s while tfm_spm links platform_s, so spm_ipc.c and tfm_hal_platform.c see the same value. That was verified on the generated compile lines - present on spm_ipc.o in m5gl2, absent in m5gl1i - rather than inferred from the CMake, which is the method D113 asked for and D114 did not fully apply.

Method note

D113 said "read the compile line before trusting the source." D114 said "enumerate what else the translation unit depends on." Both were applied here and both were still insufficient, because the remaining failure modes are about interpreting the compile line:

  • a macro absent from it may be unset rather than unplumbed (item 2);
  • two TUs may legitimately see different values, so a macro's effect is a property of the pair of guards, not of either one (item 3);
  • a guard combination that no build in C:\b exercises has no evidence behind it at all, however obviously correct it reads.

The useful generalisation is narrower than either predecessor: **an unconditional #define of a config macro whose implementation is conditionally compiled is a latent link error**, and the configuration that exposes it is by definition one nobody builds.

Carried

  • The four IAR trees are the only unrun work: m5il2, m5il3, m2il2, m2il3. All four were built in the same batch as the four green GNUARM trees and carry both defines at the right level, verified in their build.ninja. IAR has produced defects GNUARM did not four times on this port (D083, D089, D107, D108), so these are not a formality.
  • L1+IPC links and builds clean on both parts now, but has not been run. The original HardFault in arch_attempt_schedule (backend_ipc.c:517) predates every fix; with TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL defined, level 1 takes the == 1 arm and privileged is true as upstream intends, which is the standing hypothesis. Unproven until the rebuilt tree runs. L1+IPC is still not a shipping configuration.
  • RA8M2 isolation 3's non-secure half has not been captured.
  • The hook and the region dump remain enabled at isolation 2 and above on both ports. They produced D113, D114 and items 1 and 3 of this entry; they are still diagnostics.

D116 — the L1+IPC HardFault was the same undefined macro; closes D113/D114/D115's carried items

Date: 2026-10-21 · Status: Accepted · Builds on: D113, D114, D115 · Evidence: Closes carried items in D113, D114, D115; RA8M2 measured

Two runs, both of which were explicitly listed as unproven in D115.

1. L1 + IPC is green, and the hypothesis was right

**RA8M2 at isolation 1 with the IPC backend, GNUARM — secure 9/9, non-secure 7/7, both FLIH tests PASSED.** This configuration had HardFaulted since it was first attempted, on the PendSV write in arch_attempt_schedule() (backend_ipc.c:517), precise BusFault, BFAR 0xE000ED04.

D113 recorded the fault and could not explain it; D114 and D115 carried the standing hypothesis that it was the same undefined TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL, because with the macro undefined #if TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL == 1 is false and the HAL falls through to privileged = IS_PSA_ROT() - de-privileging ARoT partitions at a level where upstream intends true for every partition. Nothing was changed for this run beyond the fixes already in D113-D115, and the configuration now passes end to end. Hypothesis confirmed.

Worth stating plainly because D114 flagged it as a gap: the hypothesis never explained why L1+IPC failed earlier in boot than L2 did, and that is still not explained from first principles - it is simply consistent. An unprivileged thread reaching the PendSV write in the scheduler faults sooner than one reaching a peripheral in a test body, which is the obvious reading, but no one instrumented it. The configuration passes; the boot-order question is closed by irrelevance, not by analysis.

L1+IPC remains a configuration this port does not ship. Its value was diagnostic and it has now delivered it.

2. The hook gate confirmed at run time, not just at link time

D115 fixed CONFIG_TFM_POST_PARTITION_INIT_HOOK by gating it on CONFIG_TFM_ENABLE_MEMORY_PROTECT and verified the result by linking and by comparing binaries. The run adds the behavioural half:

TF-M isolation level is: 0x00000001
#### Execute test suites for the Secure area ####     <- no [MPU] lines anywhere

No region dump at all, which is correct and is the point: both the in-init ra_mpu_report() and the post-partition hook sit inside CONFIG_TFM_ENABLE_MEMORY_PROTECT, so at isolation 1 the whole diagnostic compiles out. A dump appearing here would have meant the gate was wrong in the other direction.

Note the banner reads Booting TF-M v2.2.0+4c9a9e687, the commit before c690534cc. The binary was built from the working tree before that commit was made, and c690534cc committed exactly what had been built - so the version string understates the content. Anyone reading this log later should not conclude the binary predates the fixes.

3. RA8M2 isolation 3, non-secure half

Captured: 7/7 suites PASSED, TFM_NS_IRQ_TEST_FLIH_1101 and 1102 included. With D115's secure-side result, RA8M2 is now fully green at isolation 1+IPC, 2 and 3, matching RA6M5. D115's "isolation 3's non-secure half has not been captured" is closed.

RA8M2 GNUARMgreengreengreengreen

  • The four IAR trees remain the substantive unrun work: m5il2, m5il3, m2il2, m2il3. Unchanged from D115 - built in the same batch as the green GNUARM trees, both defines verified present in each build.ninja. IAR has produced defects GNUARM did not four times on this port (D083, D089, D107, D108).
  • RA6M5 L1+IPC (m5gl1i) is built but unrun. RA8M2 passing makes a failure there unlikely, but the original fault was observed on both parts, so only one of the two is actually closed.
  • The hook and region dump remain enabled at isolation 2 and above on both ports. Every entry from D113 to this one depended on them; they are still diagnostics and still want a decision before the port is called done.

D117 — six corrections from an external review: D113 overstated FLIH, D116 closed a question that was answerable, and three ports deny the IDAU exists

Date: 2026-10-21 · Status: Accepted · Corrects: D113, D115, D116 · Evidence: source- and configure-verified

An outside read of the port and of D113-D116 produced seven claims. Six held. They are recorded together because the pattern behind them matters more than any one of them: every one is a case of **a true observation written down as a more general statement than the evidence supported.**

1. D113's FLIH claim was over-general

D113 states: *"TF-M runs FLIH handlers in THREAD mode at the partition's privilege, not Handler mode."* It was written to correct the opposite error and overshot. interrupt.c:195-209 picks one of three dispatches:

ConditionCallMode
TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL == 1flih_func() directlyHandler - privileged
above 1, tfm_hal_boundary_need_switch() false (PSA-RoT)flih_func() directlyHandler - privileged
above 1, switch needed (ARoT)tfm_flih_deprivileged_handling()Thread - partition's privilege

Handler mode is the usual case. Thread mode happens for an **ARoT partition at isolation 2 or 3** - exactly the FLIH test fixture D113 was measuring, hence the correct observation and the wrong generalisation.

Nothing in the port is broken by this. The fixture writes only AGT0 from the handler and does the ICU/NVIC clears in the vector entry, which is the narrowest of the three cases and so correct in all of them. Four comments and ADDING_FSP_MODULES.md §7 now state the condition instead of the rule.

2. D116 closed a question that had an answer

D116 said the hypothesis *"never explained why L1+IPC failed earlier in boot than L2 did, and that is still not explained from first principles"*, and closed it **"by irrelevance, not by analysis."** That was premature. There is a mechanism, in the same two files:

  • backend_ipc.c:169-170. At TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL == 1 the SPM gives every partition psa_api_thread_fn_call - the Thread-mode call ABI, where SPM code runs at the caller's privilege instead of going through SVC.
  • platform_s disagreed about the level. With the macro undefined there, the HAL had already taken privileged = IS_PSA_ROT() and de-privileged ARoT partitions.
  • So SPM code ran unprivileged, and arch_attempt_schedule() stores to SCB_ICSR_ADDR (tfm_arch.c, store at line 90) - 0xE000ED04, in the PPB, privileged-only by architecture. Precise BusFault, BFAR 0xE000ED04. Exactly the dump.

The crux is an asymmetry D113 missed, and it points the opposite way to what was assumed. TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL does reach the SPM: backend_ipc.o and interrupt.o both compile with -DTFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL=1, verified on m2gl1i's generated compile lines - the tree that just ran green. tfm_spm picks up psa_interface transitively. Only platform_s missed it. The two halves acted on different values of the same macro: the SPM as configured, the HAL as though the level were 0.

That answers the boot-order question directly. At isolation 1 the fault lands **inside the SPM on the first psa_* call from an ARoT partition**. At isolation 2 the SPM hands out psa_api_svc instead for any partition needing a boundary switch, so execution survives into a test body and faults later at a peripheral. Earlier failure, same root cause.

Still a source-reading account rather than a measurement: the pre-fix binary was overwritten and nobody re-ran it under instrumentation. It is consistent with every recorded symptom and with the fix working, which is as far as the evidence goes.

3. Three ports' target_cfg.c deny the existence of the IDAU

/* RA6M5 doesn't have IDAU - security attribution is done entirely via SAU */

Backwards on both halves, and present in ra6e1, ra6m4 and ra6m5 - ra6e1's copy even names RA6M4, having been pasted from it. Read off the device headers:

Part__SAUREGION_PRESENTAttribution
ra6e1, ra6m4, ra6m50 - no SAU at allIDAU, fixed by RDPM before the core runs
ra8m21SAU, programmed in bl2_boot_hal.c

The port's own tree already contradicted it: ra8m2/bl2_boot_hal.c says *"RA6M5 needs none of this. __SAUREGION_PRESENT is 0 there - no SAU at all."* ra8m2/target_cfg.c is correct for its part and was left alone. The mpc_init_cfg() and ppc_init_cfg() comments repeated the error in passing and are corrected too.

Harmless at run time - sau_and_idau_cfg() is a no-op on these parts either way, which is precisely how a wrong comment sat there through a working port. It is a documentation defect about a part's security architecture, which is the kind that gets believed.

4. D115 guessed at the PXN provenance

D115 corrected D114's claim that TFM_PXN_ENABLE never becomes a compile definition, but dated nothing. The review supplied d90aa0c44 (2023-03-14), which is also not right. Actual history of platform/CMakeLists.txt:126:

CommitDateWhat
d839593bf2021-02-25introduced it - "TZ: Add configuration switch for PXN"
ec27c23f52022-07-25moved it when the SPM HAL sources moved to tfm_spm
d90aa0c442023-03-14last touched - added the armv8.1-m.main check only

The mechanism has worked since 2021, not 2023. d90aa0c44 is the most recent edit to the line, which is what git log -L shows first and is easy to mistake for the origin.

Now confirmed by configuring rather than by reading, which D115 explicitly had not done: a TFM_PXN_ENABLE=ON configure of renesas/ra8m2 passes the armv8.1-m.main gate at check_config.cmake:91 and puts -DTFM_PXN_ENABLE on tfm_hal_isolation_v8m.o's compile line, alongside the TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL and CONFIG_TFM_PARTITION_META added by D113/D114. PXN stays OFF here - no measurement argues for it - but it is a live option, not dead code. What is still unmeasured is the effect: nobody has run a PXN build to see six static regions.

5. Two documents still describe the flash arrangement D091 replaced

CONFIGURATION.md §3 listed DEFAULT_MCUBOOT_FLASH_MAP and DEFAULT_MCUBOOT_FLASH_BACKEND as OFF/OFF with "both parts take the map and backend from FSP", citing D079, D082, D090 - the exact three entries D091 supersedes. RA8M2_SOLUTION.md's header said the same, citing D073, D076, D079.

Both were stale on two counts, because neither variable is set in either config.cmake any more and neither part supplies a flash_map_backend.h or sysflash.h. Current state: the map is ON by upstream default, DEFAULT_MCUBOOT_FLASH_BACKEND no longer exists, and RA8M2's SAU programming moved out of FSP's flash_area_open() into bl2_boot_hal.c.

DESIGN.md §4 was already correct and is now what both documents point at. Worth noting which document stayed right: the one that explains why, not the two that tabulate what.

6. UPSTREAM_CHANGES.md is not 15 live defects

It is 15 items, of which 10 are live upstream defect fixes (1-6, 9-12):

  • 13 is WITHDRAWN - D091 withdrew it.
  • 14 was already labelled report-only; 15 met the same condition but carried no label. Now labelled, with the asymmetry from item 2 above added as the sharper statement of the defect.
  • 7 (TFM_SPM_DEBUG_TRACE as a documented option) and 8 (.srec for every toolchain) are additions, not defect fixes.

One open question rather than a correction: the Submission notes group items 7, 8 and 9 together as "not labelled but belong in the same series". If 7 and 8 are additions, item 9 ("BL2 signing depends on the target, not the image file") deserves re-reading - it is written as a defect but grouped with features.

The claim that did not hold, and why it is worth recording

The review warned that its line numbers came from a tree with uncommitted port changes and would need rechecking "after a TF-M or FSP version bump". Right in spirit, wrong in detail: those changes are committed (c690534cc), an FSP bump cannot affect any of these citations because every one is in a TF-M file, and the split that matters is a different one:

  • platform/CMakeLists.txt:126, backend_ipc.c:169-170, interrupt.c:195-209, tfm_arch.c:88-90 are upstream files this port does not touch - they drift only on a TF-M uprev.
  • ra6m5/target_cfg.c:41 and ra6m5/CMakeLists.txt:515 are port files, and the latter was already invalidated by D115's own edit before the review was written.

A blanket "recheck after a version bump" would have let the already-broken citation through.

Method note

Six corrections, one pattern: a correct observation generalised past its evidence. D113 saw an ARoT handler in Thread mode and wrote a rule about FLIH. D114 saw PXN absent from a compile line and wrote a rule about the macro. D116 failed to explain a boot ordering and wrote the question off. Three ports saw sau_and_idau_cfg() work and wrote down why, wrongly.

D113 asked for "read the compile line before trusting the source" and D114 for "enumerate what else the TU depends on". This entry adds the rule that would have caught all six: **write down the case you measured, not the rule you infer from it** - and when a rule is genuinely wanted, state what would falsify it.

Carried

  • The four IAR trees (m5il2, m5il3, m2il2, m2il3) and RA6M5 L1+IPC (m5gl1i) remain unrun, unchanged from D116.
  • Item 9's classification in UPSTREAM_CHANGES.md is unresolved (item 6 above).
  • PXN's effect is unverified - the plumbing is confirmed, the six-region outcome is not.
  • Nothing here was re-measured on silicon, and nothing needed to be: every change in this entry is to a comment or a document, except the PXN configure, which was done in a throwaway tree (C:\b\pxnchk). The green runs in D115 and D116 are unaffected.

D118 — first IAR run above isolation 1: RA8M2 L2 green, and the MMIO region is the only toolchain-invariant in the table

Date: 2026-10-21 · Status: Accepted · Builds on: D113 · Evidence: RA8M2 measured; partially closes the IAR item carried since D113

**Result: RA8M2 at isolation 2, IAR 10.10.2 — secure 9/9, non-secure 7/7, both FLIH tests PASSED.** Every entry from D113 to D117 carried "the four IAR trees are rebuilt but not yet run" as the substantive open item, on the grounds that IAR has produced defects GNUARM did not four times on this port (D083, D089, D107, D108). It produced none this time. One of the four is closed; m5il2, m5il3 and m2il3 remain.

The region table, both toolchains, same part and level

Sizes in bytes, computed as limit - base + 0x20 because the dump prints RLAR masked to bits [31:5]:

idxRegionGNUARMIARdelta
0combined unprivileged/ARoT code21,15223,552+2,400
1PSA RoT code225,760219,648-6,112
2RO data37,60041,536+3,936
3App RoT data5,3125,248-64
4PSA RoT data58,91259,264+352
5AGT0 (MMIO)2562560 - byte-identical
total348,992349,504+512

idx 5 is identical in base and limit; every other region differs. That is exactly the right invariant and is the useful result here. Regions 0-4 are derived from linker symbols, so they move with whatever the toolchain decides about section placement and padding. Region 5 comes from tfm_peripherals_def.c's platform_data_t - a literal base and limit in port source - so it cannot move, and it does not. The MMIO path that D113 found broken is therefore toolchain-independent, which was not previously demonstrated: every measurement behind D113-D117 was GNUARM.

Both toolchains also pack the table tightly: all ten regions 32-byte aligned, and every adjacent pair inside the same memory area exactly 0x20 apart, with no slack.

What this does and does not cover

Covered: the two defines reaching platform_s under IAR, the MMIO region being programmed at bind time, an unprivileged ARoT partition reaching its peripheral, and the FLIH path including the privileged/unprivileged split across tfm_timer0_irq.c and plat_test.c.

Not covered: isolation 3 under IAR on either part, which is where the CONFIG_TFM_PARTITION_META arm from D114 lives. Level 2 takes the != 3 branch and cannot exercise it, so the metadata-pointer region remains GNUARM-only evidence. m2il3 is the single most informative tree still unrun.

Carried

  • Three IAR trees unrun: m5il2, m5il3, m2il3. m2il3 and m5il3 carry the only untested arm of D114's fix.
  • RA6M5 L1+IPC (m5gl1i) still unrun - unchanged from D116/D117.
  • Item 9's classification in UPSTREAM_CHANGES.md is still unresolved (D117 item 6).

Date: 2026-10-21 · Status: Accepted · Builds on: D118 · Evidence: closes the gap D118 named; RA8M2 measured

**Result: RA8M2 at isolation 3, IAR 10.10.2 — secure 9/9, non-secure 7/7, both FLIH tests PASSED.** D118 identified m2il3 as "the single most informative tree still unrun" because level 2 takes the != 3 branch and therefore cannot exercise CONFIG_TFM_PARTITION_META. It has now run, and it does exercise it:

Both arms of D114's fix are now confirmed on both toolchains, which was the last piece of that entry carrying only GNUARM evidence.
