D120 — the isolation-macro gap is this port's, not upstream's; D113's root cause was wrong and upstream item 15 is withdrawn

Date: 2026-10-22 · Status: Accepted · Corrects: D065, D113, D117 · Evidence: Withdraws UPSTREAM_CHANGES.md item 15; an519 measured

An external documentation review (findings F014, F196, F200) challenged the root cause recorded in D113 and repeated in D114, D117, upstream item 15 and four port comments. It was right, and verifying it produced a sharper answer than the review itself reached.

What D113 said, and why it is wrong

D113: *"platform_s links tfm_config, not psa_interface ... So platform/ext/common/tfm_hal_isolation_v8m.c ... compiles with it undefined on every platform using the shared HAL."*

The first clause is true. The conclusion does not follow, because nothing obliges the shared HAL to be compiled into platform_s at all. That is a per-platform choice, and this port is the outlier:

PlatformAdds tfm_hal_isolation_v8m.c toMacros arrive?
an519, an524, corstone300, corstone310, mps4, musca_b1, musca_s1, rse, alcortfm_spmyes
ra6e1, ra6m4, ra6m5, ra8m2platform_sno

tfm_spm links psa_interface; platform_s links tfm_config. **Nine upstream users out of nine put it in tfm_spm. All four RA ports put it in platform_s.**

Measured, to the standard D113 itself demanded. an519 configured at isolation 2:

object: secure_fw/spm/CMakeFiles/tfm_spm.dir/__/__/platform/ext/common/tfm_hal_isolation_v8m.o
flags : -DTFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL=2  -DCONFIG_TFM_PARTITION_META  -DCONFIG_TFM_ENABLE_MEMORY_PROTECT

All three present. There is no upstream defect.

The attest-HAL setting contributes but is not the trigger

The review's own account stopped here, and it is worth recording why it is incomplete. platform_s PRIVATE-links tfm_sprt, which PUBLIC-links psa_interface, but only when PLATFORM_DEFAULT_ATTEST_HAL is ON (platform/CMakeLists.txt:109; default ON at config/config_base.cmake:116). Exactly six platforms set it OFF: mps4, rse and the four RA ports.

So for this port the macros are blocked twice over - wrong target, and the one edge that would have rescued it switched off. But mps4 sets it OFF and is fine, because it uses tfm_spm. The target choice is the cause; the attest-HAL setting is why there is no accidental backstop.

(rse is not exposed either way - it supplies its own tfm_hal_isolation_rse.c.)

Correction to D114: "with both undefined, neither arm fires"

D114 and the old item 15 both say that with both macros undefined, neither arm of

#if   TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL != 3        /* App RoT data region   */
#elif defined(CONFIG_TFM_PARTITION_META)  /* TFM_SP_META_PTR region */
#endif

fires. False. Undefined evaluates to 0, 0 != 3 is true, so the App RoT data arm fires and the #elif is never reached - which is exactly why isolation 2 behaved sanely and why D113's dump showed the App RoT data region present.

"Neither arm fires" describes a different state: after D113's fix had defined TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL=3, while CONFIG_TFM_PARTITION_META was still missing. That is the four-region dump and the MMFAR 0x20000400 fault D114 recorded. The finding stands; the stated precondition was wrong, and it was wrong in two documents.

Corollary worth keeping: with both undefined, level 3 would have built five static regions and every #if TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL == 3 block - bind index, per-switch reprogramming, MIN_NR_PRIVATE_DATA_REGION - would have compiled out silently.

What changed

  • UPSTREAM_CHANGES.md item 15 → WITHDRAWN, with the an519 measurement. Live upstream defect fixes remain 10 (items 1-6, 9-12); the list now has two withdrawn entries, 13 and 15.
  • ra6m5 and ra8m2 CMakeLists.txt: the "an upstream gap, and a silent one" comment replaced with the target table and the measurement. RA8M2's copy also stopped citing RA6M5's AGT0 address as its own.
  • The port's target_compile_definitions(platform_s PRIVATE ...) fix is **unchanged and still correct**. Only the explanation was wrong.

Still open

  • ra6e1 and ra6m4 have neither define and compile the shared HAL into platform_s, so they carry the same gap unfixed. Harmless while they only run isolation 1 + SFN - no MPU regions are programmed there at all - but it is latent, and it is the same two lines.
  • Moving the source to tfm_spm would delete the deviation instead of documenting it, and match all nine upstream users. Untried. It touches four ports' build files, so it is a decision, not a cleanup.

The RA6M4 brick cause is contested in this log, and D094 wins

Recorded here because the course review hit it and it will be hit again. D065 (2026-09-29) names PBPS at 0x0100A1E0 as "the exact word that destroyed two EK-RA6M4 boards". D094 (2026-10-06) says "which zeroed field killed the boards is still unknown", having disproved FSPR permanence (no Flash Access Window on RA6M4) and OFS1_SEL content (byte-identical on a working board). D094 is later and is the operative entry: **PBPS is the surviving candidate, not a finding.** DESIGN.md §8.4 still describes the withdrawn FSPR mechanism and needs correcting.

Neither the mechanism nor the guidance depends on this: the coalesced zero-filled PT_LOAD is proven byte-exact, and the rules - one MEMORY region per option word, audit readelf -l, flash .elf/.hex never .bin - are unaffected.

Method note

D113 said "read the compile line before trusting the source". It did read the compile line - and saw a macro absent. D117 then added that a missing -D does not distinguish unset from unplumbed, after the PXN error. This entry adds the third member of the family:

**A missing -D also does not tell you whether the file was supposed to be compiled by that target at all.** The compile line answers "what did this object get"; it cannot answer "is this the object upstream builds". Checking that needed one question nobody asked for five rounds - which target do the other platforms add this source to? - and it is a single grep.

D121 — the shared isolation HAL moves to tfm_spm; D113's workaround is deleted, not documented

Date: 2026-10-22 · Status: Accepted · Builds on: D120 · Evidence: Implements the option D120 left open; ra6m5, ra8m2, ra6e1; built, not yet re-run

D120 established that the isolation HAL missed TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL and CONFIG_TFM_PARTITION_META because this port compiles it into platform_s, while all nine upstream users compile it into tfm_spm. That entry left the obvious consequence as an open decision. Taken:

target_sources(tfm_spm
    PRIVATE
        ${PLATFORM_DIR}/ext/common/tfm_hal_isolation_v8m.c
)

and the target_compile_definitions(platform_s PRIVATE ...) workaround from D113/D114 is deleted. Net -122/+84 lines across three ports, most of it comment that no longer needs to exist.

Why this and not the two defines

The defines fixed the two macros someone had already been bitten by. D114's own lesson - "enumerate what else the translation unit depends on" - exists only because the first fix was instance-shaped. Linking the file where upstream links it fixes the class: every definition psa_interface carries arrives, including any it gains later, and nobody has to re-audit this file's #ifs on an uprev.

Scope, and the part left out

PortMovedRebuiltRun
ra6m5yes5 trees (L1i/L2/L3 GNUARM, L2/L3 IAR)not yet
ra8m2yes4 trees (L1i/L2/L3 GNUARM, L2/L3 IAR)not yet
ra6e1yesfresh GNUARM buildno - and not planned
ra6m4no--

ra6m4 is deliberately untouched: both EK-RA6M4 boards are dead (D094), so a change there could not be verified even in principle. It keeps the gap, and keeps no defines either.

ra6e1 is a behavioural change that will not be tested. It had neither define, so its HAL took privileged = IS_PSA_ROT() at isolation 1, de-privileging ARoT partitions where upstream intends true for every partition - the same mis-evaluation behind the L1+IPC fault in D117. It now receives TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL=1 and takes the == 1 arm. That should be a correction, and it is the configuration upstream ships, but it is asserted from source, not measured.

What was verified, and what was not

Verified, all nine regression trees plus a fresh ra6e1 configure:

  • the HAL object is tfm_spm.dir/.../tfm_hal_isolation_v8m.o in every one;
  • TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL, CONFIG_TFM_PARTITION_META and CONFIG_TFM_ENABLE_MEMORY_PROTECT are all on its compile line, with nothing hand-defined;
  • every tree builds and links clean, GNUARM and IAR.

The programmed MPU table is unchanged, with one exception. Comparing the PT_* boundary symbols the static table is built from:

TreePT_* boundaries
m5gl2, m2gl2, m2gl3identical, 36 symbols each
m2il2, m2il3match the values read off the hardware runs in D118/D119
m5gl3PT_PSA_ROT_CODE_END and PT_RO_DATA_START 0x000D8400→0x000D8420, PT_RO_DATA_END 0x000E5D80→0x000E5DA0

Same region sizes; three boundaries moved one 32-byte granule because the net code-size change crossed an alignment boundary in that configuration only. **RA6M5 at isolation 3 will therefore print two different numbers than D114 recorded.** That is expected, not a regression.

The code itself moved from .ER_PSA_ROT_CODE (-16 B) to .ER_TFM_CODE (+24 B) - out of the PSA-RoT code region into the SPM's own. Both are privileged and MPU_CTRL.PRIVDEFENA is set (CTRL reads 7), so privileged execution is unaffected, and it is where upstream puts it.

Not verified: anything on silicon. Nine green runs (D113-D119) were made against the old arrangement. The symbol evidence says the MPU programming is unchanged on three of four GNUARM trees and on both RA8M2 IAR trees, which makes a re-run confirmation rather than discovery - but it is still owed before this is called done.

Consequences for the record

  • UPSTREAM_CHANGES.md item 15 was already WITHDRAWN by D120; this removes the last reason anyone would reopen it. The port no longer deviates here at all.
  • The long "a PORT gap, NOT an upstream one" comment in ra6m5/ra8m2 is replaced by a short note on why the placement is load-bearing, with the measured symptoms kept as the reason not to move it back.

Method note - two false passes in one verification

Both of this entry's comparisons initially reported success while comparing nothing:

  1. a grep -E pattern for PT_[A-Z_]*_(START|END)\$\$Base died on shell quoting (grep: Trailing backslash), so diff compared two empty sets and printed no differences;
  2. the rewritten Python check normalised GCC's Image$$PT_x$$Base but not IAR's PT_x$$Base, so every expected key landed in "missing" while the script still printed MATCHES.

Both were caught only because the output carried a warning or an oddly-shaped field, not because the check failed. The rule this earns: **a comparison that reports "no differences" must also report how many items it compared, and a count of zero is a failure, not a pass.** Both checks now print compared N/M. This is the same family as D113's "read the compile line" and D120's "ask which target compiles the file" - the tooling will happily confirm whatever you forgot to ask it.

D122 — the tfm_spm move is MPU-neutral on silicon, and RA6M5 L1+IPC is green for the first time — cause unexplained

Date: 2026-10-22 · Status: Accepted · Builds on: D121 · Evidence: partially discharges D121's "not yet re-run"; RA6M5 measured

Two runs on the post-move binaries (D121, banner a3472cc47).

1. Isolation 2 — the prediction holds, byte for byte

RA6M5 at isolation 2, GNUARM — secure 9/9 PASSED. The post-partition dump:

  idx 0  0x000A0400 - 0x000A5640      idx 3  0x20000400 - 0x200018A0
  idx 1  0x000A5660 - 0x000D82E0      idx 4  0x200018C0 - 0x20011480
  idx 2  0x000D8300 - 0x000E5BC0      idx 5  0x400E8000 - 0x400E80E0   AGT0

Identical to D113's dump in all six regions, including AGT0's MMIO entry. D121 predicted exactly this from the PT_* boundary symbols; silicon agrees. Moving the HAL from platform_s to tfm_spm changes which archive the object comes from and nothing the MPU sees.

2. Isolation 1 + IPC on RA6M5 — green, and that is the surprise

Secure 9/9 PASSED, TF-M isolation level is: 0x00000001, no [MPU] lines (correct - the dump is inside CONFIG_TFM_ENABLE_MEMORY_PROTECT, which is undefined at level 1).

This configuration has never passed on this part. Its history:

WhenBuildResult
pre-D113no isolation macros at allHardFault in arch_attempt_schedule, BFAR 0xE000ED04
D117, 2026-10-21macros via target_compile_definitions(platform_s)still failed - parked in BL2's weak HardFault_Handler at 0xa84, nothing on RTT
this entrymacros via tfm_spm (D121)passes

The honest position: the cause is not established. The failing build of 2026-10-21 already had -DTFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL=1 on the HAL's compile line - that was verified at the time - so the macro was not what changed. The only source delta between that build and this one is the target move, and **no mechanism is known by which compiling the same file into a different archive cures a fault that parks in BL2's handler before any TF-M output appears.**

Two readings, and the evidence does not separate them:

  • the move fixed something real, by a route nobody has traced;
  • the 2026-10-21 failure was transient - a stale or partial flash - and was never a code fault at all. The launch was proved identical to the working L2 one, bl2.bin proved byte-identical to the L2 tree's, and the build was clean, which is consistent with this reading.

The second is the more economical explanation and the port should not bank on the first. What would settle it: reflash the pre-move m5gl1i image and see whether it still parks at 0xa84. That image has been overwritten, so settling it means rebuilding at the previous commit.

Either way, L1+IPC remains a configuration this port does not ship. It was kept alive as a diagnostic, and as a diagnostic it has now produced everything it is going to.

D125 — six corrections to D120–D123 from the second documentation review; the HAL never left the PSA-RoT code region

Date: 2026-10-22 · Status: Accepted · Corrects: D120, D121, D122, D123 · Evidence: source-verified

A second pass of the external documentation review (findings F237, F241, F243, F245-F252) was run against fsp_cmake b821e3f and TF-M addc59f54. It also withdrew its own first-pass explanation of the macro gap and confirmed D120's. Six of its findings land on entries of mine. All six hold.

1. The code did not move out of the PSA-RoT code region — D121 and D123 both say it did

D121: *"The code itself moved from .ER_PSA_ROT_CODE (-16 B) to .ER_TFM_CODE (+24 B) - out of the PSA-RoT code region into the SPM's own."* The second clause is wrong. platform/ext/common/gcc/tfm_isolation_s.ld.template:

215:    Image$$PT_PSA_ROT_CODE_START$$Base = .;
250:    .ER_TFM_CODE  ALIGN(4) (READONLY) :      <- inside
320:    Image$$PT_PSA_ROT_CODE_END$$Base = .;

.ER_TFM_CODE lies between the two boundary symbols, so both sections are inside the same MPU region. The object moved between two sections of one region, and the privileged-execution argument D121 made - "both are privileged and PRIVDEFENA is set" - was answering a question that does not arise.

2. A region grew; it did not merely shift

D121 and D123 both say "same region sizes". Measured on m5gl3:

Regionpre-movepost-movesize
PSA RoT code0x000A5660..0x000D84000x000A5660..0x000D8420+32 bytes - GREW
RO data0x000D8400..0x000E5D800x000D8420..0x000E5DA0+0, shifted

The base of PSA RoT code never moves, so the +8 bytes of code landing inside it can only push the end out. That follows directly from item 1 and should have been predicted rather than contradicted. D123's three measured values are still correct; the sentence explaining them is not.

3. D121's tree count

Its scope table says ra8m2 | 4 trees. Five were rebuilt: m2gl2, m2gl3, m2gl1i, m2il2, m2il3, matching RA6M5's five. Ten trees in total, not nine.

4. D122 called two runs "green" on the secure suites alone

D122 records "RA6M5 at isolation 2 - secure 9/9 PASSED" and the same for L1+IPC, then marks both green in its coverage table. Every entry from D113 onward has meant *secure and non-secure* by "green". The non-secure halves of those two captures were truncated, so the evidence does not reach the bar the word carries elsewhere in this log. D123 and D124 report both halves and are unaffected; the L2 and L1+IPC rows in D122 should read secure-only.

5. The 2026-10-21 m5gl1i failure has no entry of its own

It appears only as a row in D122's history table. The run that produced it - PC parked in BL2's weak HardFault_Handler at 0xa84, nothing on RTT, with the launch, bl2.bin and build all proved identical or clean - is the single piece of evidence that would decide D122's open question, and it is recorded nowhere as a run. Noted here so the absence is at least deliberate.

6. Two wrong attributions in D120

  • rse. D120 says it "is not exposed either way - it supplies its own tfm_hal_isolation_rse.c". It does supply one, but that is not why it is safe: rse/common/CMakeLists.txt:612-615 adds tfm_hal_isolation_v8m.c to tfm_spm like every other upstream user. It is unaffected for the same reason they are.
  • PBPS. D120 writes "PBPS is the surviving candidate, not a finding" as though D094 said so. D094 says three explanations were offered and two disproven, and never names the third. Ranking PBPS as the survivor is an inference drawn here from D065, not a finding of D094.

What was corrected outside this entry

  • ra6m5/ra8m2 CMakeLists.txt - the "with them undefined" precondition repeated the error D120 §"Correction to D114" had already identified, in the one place nobody re-read. Now split into the two sequential states. The PXN provenance now records that d90aa0c44 removed the architecture test from the generator expression as well as adding tfm_invalid_config(); the old wording said it "only added the check".
  • PXN re-verified after the move, since the earlier measurement predated it: a TFM_PXN_ENABLE=ON configure of renesas/ra8m2 at isolation 3 puts -DTFM_PXN_ENABLE on the now-tfm_spm-owned tfm_hal_isolation_v8m.o, alongside the other two macros. It arrives by a different route - PUBLIC on platform_s, which tfm_spm links.
  • UPSTREAM_CHANGES.md item 15 - its platform table predated D121 and still listed all four RA ports under platform_s; ra6m4 is now the only one. The interface/CMakeLists.txt:37 citation covered only TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL; CONFIG_TFM_PARTITION_META is at :40.
  • DESIGN.md §8.4 - it called the mechanism "proven byte-exact" while quoting a 460-byte span. D094 measured 388 bytes (0x184) with 376 of zero fill, across the three OFS words that BL2 actually emitted. 460 is the width of the sparse map, not of any image's segment, and the guard window is wider than both.

Method note

Item 1 is the one worth keeping. D121 asserted a section had left an MPU region without opening the linker script that defines the region's bounds - while that same entry was congratulating itself on predicting MPU behaviour from symbols. The symbol evidence was right and the prose around it was invented. Items 2 and 3 are consequences: a size claim that contradicted the entry's own numbers, and a count that contradicted the entry's own list.

**Three entries in a row (D121, D122, D123) each carried a correct measurement wrapped in a wrong sentence.** The measurements were checked; the sentences were not. Checking a claim means checking the claim, not the number it sits next to.

D126 — eighteen corrections to D110–D125 from the second review; two carried items closed, and D115's "three of four corners" was wrong

Date: 2026-10-22 · Status: Accepted · Corrects: D110, D112, D113, D114, D115, D116, D117, D119, D124 · Evidence: source-verified

The second documentation review raised 18 findings against this log. All hold. They are collected here rather than as nine entries, because most are one-line factual slips and the pattern they form is worth more than any of them.

1. D115's "three of the four corners are safe" is wrong — SFN reaches the hook too

D115 explained the L1+IPC link failure by saying *"L1+SFN has no call site at all (the hook is called only from spm_ipc.c, and the SFN backend is a different file)."* **Both halves of that are false.**

  • secure_fw/spm/CMakeLists.txt:54 compiles core/spm_ipc.c unconditionally. Only backend_ipc.c and backend_sfn.c are behind backend generator expressions (:65, :66).
  • spm_ipc.c:397 defines tfm_spm_init(), which holds the hook call, and include/ffm/backend_sfn.h:14 is #define BACKEND_SPM_INIT() tfm_spm_init(). **SFN calls it.**

So L1+SFN had the caller without the body as well, and would have failed to link identically. It did not fail only because no L1+SFN tree was rebuilt between the hook being added (D113) and the gate being added (D115) — the existing L1+SFN trees predate the hook and carry no such symbol. The gate in D115 is still correct; it is more necessary than that entry argued, not less.

D124's condition was also incomplete. platform/CMakeLists.txt:125 defines CONFIG_TFM_ENABLE_MEMORY_PROTECT for TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL > 1 or TEST_PSA_API STREQUAL "IPC", so the PSA Arch IPC suite gets the body — and now the hook — at isolation 1 too. "Above isolation 1" is the wrong way to say it.

2. Line numbers

EntrySaidIs
D113, D115, D116backend_ipc.c:517:513 — :517 is the closing brace of backend_abi_leaving_spm(), and the faulting store is not in this file at all
D117, D125the ICSR store at tfm_arch.c:90:91 — :88 is the bne, :89 loads SCB_ICSR_ADDR, :90 loads the bit
D114the region missing at 0x20000400 is the App RoT data regionthe TFM_SP_META_PTR region. At level 3 the App RoT data region is never in the static set, which is the entry's own point

3. D119 described a region growth the HAL does not perform

D119 wrote that isolation 3 "grows the PSA RoT data region to cover what it gave up". Its own table refutes it: PSA RoT data goes 59,264 → 59,392 B, +128, while App RoT data gives up 5,248. The #if/#elif only swaps which of two regions occupies one slot; the +128 is layout and padding. Nothing absorbs anything.

4. Two coverage claims that outran the evidence

  • D119/D116 "RA8M2 is complete: every level this port supports". Every run behind that is regression + FLIH. The SLIH suite has never run on RA8M2 on either toolchain — D072 lists it "built, not run" and D102 records that the m2gslih trees never got a launch. The honest claim is "complete for the regression+FLIH configuration at every isolation level".
  • D116's title says it closes D113-D115's carried items. It closes two — RA8M2 L1+IPC and RA8M2 L3 non-secure. The four IAR trees, RA6M5 L1+IPC and the diagnostics decision stayed open, as D116's own Carried list says.

5. Two carried items dropped without closure

Both were carried by D114/D115/D116 and then simply absent from D117 onward:

  • The MPU diagnostics. The post-partition hook and region dump are still enabled at isolation 2 and above on both ports (ra6m5/config_tfm_target.h, ra8m2 likewise). Thirteen entries have called them temporary. Decision, recorded here: they stay. They produced D113 through D125, they cost nothing below isolation 2 and nothing at all once CONFIG_TFM_ENABLE_MEMORY_PROTECT is absent, and the alternative is re-deriving the MPU table from symbols every time someone doubts it. Remove them only with a reason better than tidiness.
  • PXN's effect. D117 carried "the plumbing is confirmed, the six-region outcome is not", then D118/D119 dropped it. It is deliberately parked: PXN stays OFF, no measurement argues for turning it on, and the plumbing was re-confirmed post-D121. Re-carried here so it is parked rather than lost.

6. Smaller corrections

  • D117 §3 and D125, on the SAU. "No SAU at all" is imprecise: an Armv8-M core with the Security Extension always implements SAU_CTRL/SAU_TYPE, and __SAUREGION_PRESENT 0 means zero regions. The IDAU decides only because FSP writes SAU_CTRL.ALLNS = 1 (bsp_security.c:277). At reset, ALLNS 0 with the SAU disabled makes every address Secure. Corrected in target_cfg.c on all three ports and in DESIGN.md §7.
  • D117 §4, d90aa0c44. It did not only add the check_config.cmake test; it also removed the armv8.1-m.main term from the generator expression at platform/CMakeLists.txt:126, moving the gate from a silent filter to an explicit failure.
  • D112 "where it came from". 2b5015c touched ten .secure_azone files, not six. And re-running the quoted command now returns 87f3fdd, D112's own fix, so the reproducibility claim holds only "before 87f3fdd".
  • D110 "the evidence is three builds". None of the three tested the combination that answers the question (__dwrite present, setvbuf absent). Rows 1-2 show buffering holds output when the backend is semihosting; they do not isolate how much each fix contributes. The conclusion may well be right; it is an inference, not a proof.
  • D119 "IAR has produced no defect above isolation 1 on this part, after four below it". Two of those four are not IAR toolchain behaviour: D083 and D089 are a stale ewarm install path frozen in CMake caches, and D083's fix covered only RA6M5. Separate the build-environment defects from D107/D108, which are IAR's.
  • D113 "r_spi 12 call sites, r_iic_master 7, r_sci_uart 5, r_canfd 5". Not reproducible from these trees — no FSP 6.7 project here contains those drivers, and the entry does not say which call set was counted. Treat the numbers as indicative; the architectural point (FSP's Open writes the NVIC, which is privileged-only) stands on R_AGT_Open alone.
  • D041 has no "superseded by D044" line, which rule 2 of this log requires and scripts/decision_threads.py --strict would flag.

7. The Settled-questions table

Three rows added, because in each the thread reverses an earlier claim and a reader who stops at the first entry gets the wrong answer:

QuestionSettled position
Does TFM_PXN_ENABLE reach the HAL?Yes — platform/CMakeLists.txt:126, PUBLIC on platform_s. D114 said "nowhere in TF-M"; corrected by D115, confirmed by configure in D117 and again post-move in D125
What mode does a FLIH handler run in?Handler, except an ARoT partition at isolation 2 or 3, which is Thread. D113 stated the exception as the rule; D117 corrected it
Why did the isolation HAL miss its macros?Because this port compiled it into platform_s; all nine upstream users compile it into tfm_spm. D113 blamed upstream, D120 corrected it, D121 moved the file

Method note

Of the eighteen, nine are wrong line numbers or counts and six are claims that were true of the case measured and written down as general. Only D115's corner analysis is a reasoning error, and it has the same shape as D121's: **an explanation invented to fit a result that had already been obtained by other means.** The gate was right because the link failed and stopped failing; the story about which four corners were safe was constructed afterwards and never checked against secure_fw/spm/CMakeLists.txt, which would have taken one grep.

D125 said "checking a claim means checking the claim, not the number it sits next to". The narrower version: **when an entry explains why something failed, check the explanation against the build files, not against the symptom it was written to explain.**

D127 — the CMake target graph gets its own document, drawn in ASCII rather than mermaid

Date: 2026-10-22 · Status: Accepted · Builds on: D121, D126 · Evidence: generator and renderer read; four reviewed facts corrected against source

Nothing in the document set drew the build graph. DESIGN.md §1 says why the port consumes RASC, ADDING_FSP_MODULES.md says how to add one module, and UPSTREAM_CHANGES.md lists the patches — but which target links which, with what scope, was only ever reconstructed by grep. That reconstruction is exactly what D113 through D126 spent ~990 log lines on, and it had to be done three times before it came out right. BUILD_ARCHITECTURE.md records it.

Why ASCII and not mermaid. docs/learning/ is plain HTML opened from disk, and build_doc_html.py deliberately escapes every < and has no raw-HTML passthrough (its docstring: stdlib only, so the hook has no dependency to install). Supporting mermaid means either a CDN script in pages meant to work offline, or vendoring megabytes of mermaid.min.js. Fenced ASCII renders correctly in the course HTML, on GitHub, in VSCode and in a terminal, with no renderer change. The pretty version exists as a published artifact; the repo copy is the one that cannot rot.

Four claims corrected against source while writing it — each had been stated from memory and each was wrong:

ClaimActually
bl2 links platform_bl2it does not. bl2 → bootutil → platform_bl2, both PUBLIC (bl2/ext/mcuboot/CMakeLists.txt:70, :30). The executable never names it
BL2 is signed like the other two imagesBL2 is the root of trust and is flashed raw. Only tfm_s and tfm_ns go through imgtool
the FSP module libraries are PRIVATE on the platform targetsPUBLIC — ra6m5/CMakeLists.txt:371 and :665
FSP_MODULES_NEVER_BUILT excludes modules from the buildit is the allowlist for the unclaimed-directory audit (:278), which emits a WARNING. The hard failure is a name in FSP_MODULES_* with no cmake/modules/fsp_<name>.cmake, because include() is not OPTIONAL. Two different mistakes, two different outcomes

Consistent with D126's method note: all four were memory restating a plausible shape, and all four took one grep to settle. The new document cites file and line on every edge for that reason — a reader who doubts a line can check it without rebuilding the graph.

D128 — the metadata line is an index and may be repaired in place (new rule 7); ten relation fields corrected, and D120/D125/D126 each got one attribution wrong

Date: 2026-10-22 · Status: Accepted · Corrects: D120, D125, D126 · Evidence: third documentation review (artifacts_v3), F246/F257/F258/F292–F295/F299/F300; all ten verified against the entries they name

The third review raised the governance question this log had been dodging and found that the generated index had been wrong in eight ways, most of them introduced by the normalisation in c0d6450 that was supposed to make it reliable.

1. The rule question (F300), answered

c0d6450 rewrote the metadata line of 91 entries and inserted Date/Status lines into 15 (D019–D025, D057–D064), against a file whose rule 1 reads *"Entries are never edited once written."* That was a real contradiction, not a technicality, and it is the commit that introduced the D090 and D093 errors below.

Resolved by distinguishing the record from the index, now rule 7. Rules 1 and 4 exist to protect the reasoning — "silent repair destroys the record of having believed it". A relation field records no belief; it is a pointer, read only by the two generators. Rule 2 already appends to it. So the prose stays immutable and the index becomes repairable, with every repair named in the entry that found it. The alternative — appending an entry for each index error and teaching the generators to chase it — makes the index unqueryable to protect something that was never reasoning.

Nothing in c0d6450 touched an entry body. That was true then and is now the stated boundary.

2. The ten fields corrected

EntryWasNowWhy

Closes is a new relation, and the last three are why. D008 and D014 are Provisional; D029's title is literally OPEN DEFECT. Each was shut by a later entry that recorded the fact as Builds on — the one relation meaning the earlier entry is untouched. So SETTLED.md listed "OPEN DEFECT: .ram_from_flash is excluded from copy-init" in its Standing table, with the title as the current position, five weeks after D048 fixed it. That is the worst failure this index can have: not a stale detail, but pointing a reader at a closed defect as live. Closes says the entry's status is historical while its reasoning stands — neither Supersedes (not replaced) nor Corrects (nothing in it was wrong). Like Corrects it forms no lineage: D029 and D048 answer different questions. The generator strikes the status through and names the closing entry.

3. D120's "Correction to D114" was aimed at the wrong target (F246)

D120 attributes to D114 a claim that with both macros undefined neither arm fires, and corrects it. D114 does not say that. It is explicitly the isolation-3 run taken after D113's TFM_ISOLATION_LEVEL fix, and what it writes of CONFIG_TFM_PARTITION_META is "Undefined, neither arm fires" — which is the state D120 itself calls correct.

The "both undefined" error existed in exactly one place: UPSTREAM_CHANGES.md item 15 (e686c71:347). D114's statement was right for its run. Under rule 2 a reader would have treated D114 as discredited, so D114 is removed from D120's Corrects list; D120's prose keeps the section, and this entry is what a reader following the index now reaches.

4. D125 §4 holds D122 to a bar D123 does not clear either

D125 §4 ruled that D122 called two runs "green" on secure evidence alone, and added that "D123 and D124 report both halves and are unaffected". D123 §2 says of its own RA6M5 IAR isolation-2 run: *"The secure suite also passed; its RTT output was not captured, so the secure half is reported rather than recorded here."* That is the same gap, stated plainly by D123 itself, in the same review pass that found it in D122. D123's IAR L2 cell should carry the same qualification its L3 GNUARM cell does not need.

5. D126 §6's last bullet was wrong, and so were two of its attributions (F295)

  • D041. D126 says it "has no 'superseded by D044' line, which rule 2 of this log requires". D044 carries Corrects: [D041] with the evidence "supersedes the second fix in D041 only" — and Corrects is the right relation, because D044 drops one of three fixes and leaves the rest standing. The relation was never missing. Nothing to fix.
  • D125 twice. D126 §2 attributes the tfm_arch.c:90 line number to "D117, D125", and §6 attributes SAU wording to "D117 §3 and D125". D125 contains no occurrence of tfm_arch, :90, :91, SAU, IDAU or ICSR. Both corrections land on D117 alone, so D125 is removed from D126's Corrects list and D124 — which §1 does correct — added.

Method note

D126 closed by saying: *when an entry explains why something failed, check the explanation against the build files.* Four of the five errors here are the narrower case — **an entry citing a sibling entry without opening it.** D126 attributed two corrections to D125 and a missing line to D041; D120 attributed a precondition to D114; D125 cleared D123 of a gap D123 describes in its own §2. Every one took a single search of the file this log is written in. The citation is the claim.

D129 — the v4 review of BUILD_ARCHITECTURE.md: eight findings, the FSPR attribution withdrawn in eleven more places, and line citations are now checked

Date: 2026-10-22 · Status: Accepted · Corrects: D128 · Builds on: D094, D127 · Evidence: v4 addendum F301–F308; all eight re-verified in source; check_arch_lines.py 55/55

The fourth review pass added an addendum reviewing BUILD_ARCHITECTURE.md, written one commit earlier in D127. It confirmed the link graph, all 21 port citations and the nine upstream tfm_spm users, and raised eight findings — two medium. All eight hold.

1. The two medium findings were both inherited, not invented

  • F301. "r_sce is never built; TF-M uses its own mbedcrypto; only the TRNG is taken." All three clauses are wrong on the live parts. The sce module builds r_sce (FSP_MODULE_DIRS_sce), the TRNG is always reachable, and the SCE9/RSIP-E50D cipher *_ALT path is live whenever CRYPTO_HW_ACCELERATOR is ON — the default. The crypto library is FSP's, through the fsp_mbedtls.cmake overlay. What is actually excluded is FSP's **PSA/ITS configuration**, which wires PSA ITS to littlefs.
  • F302. The tfm_ns row described a path that is off by default. The block sits inside if(FSP_NS_APP_DIR AND RA6M5_NS_IN_SPE_BUILD), OFF since 2026-08-30 and kept only for single-configure boot bisection. In the normal split build the SPE project has **no tfm_ns target at all** — which contradicted §1 and §2 of the same document.

**D127's method note said the citation is the claim. Both of these were copied from port comments without opening the module file that contradicts them.** fsp_sce.cmake's header has been correct the whole time: *"This module builds r_sce only… Secure image: the TRNG always; the cipher ALT path when CRYPTO_HW_ACCELERATOR is on."* One file away.

2. Six low findings, all confirmed

:402/:411 omitted tfm_timer0_irq.c and the FLIH/SLIH gate (F305); bl2_boot_hal.c was listed under platform_bl2 when it is added to bl2, and only under if(CRYPTO_HW_ACCELERATOR) (F306 — the review had the condition right and the target wrong); the HAL tests six macros, not four, two delivered by header and therefore target-independent (F304); the -S sources shown are the regression flow only, the application build uses the TF-M root and <part>/ns_app (F303); and "ra8m2 is the same shape" understated it — same targets, different layout and different numbers throughout (F307).

3. The FSPR attribution survived in eleven places

F308 flagged one port comment still blaming FSPR for the brick. A sweep found eleven, across all four ports: CMakeLists.txt × 4, region_defs.h × 3, *_bl2.ld × 3, *_bl2.icf × 3 — and ra6m4/CMakeLists.txt additionally told the reader to "read FAWMON/FSPR over J-Link", which D094 establishes is meaningless on a part reporting BSP_FEATURE_FLASH_SUPPORTS_ACCESS_WINDOW = 0. All corrected to "which field dies is unknown".

D094 was written 16 days before this. **Withdrawing a claim in the log does not withdraw it from the tree**, and a withdrawn diagnosis repeated in eleven load-bearing comments is the version a maintainer will actually read.

4. ra6e1 is the opposite case, and nearly got the wrong fix

ra6e1 carries the same two stale comments, and on that part they are correct: CRYPTO_HW_ACCELERATOR is OFF (config.cmake:102) and there is no fsp_mbedtls.cmake, so TF-M's own mbedcrypto really is the library and the TRNG really is all that is taken. Only the "never built" framing is wrong there. Propagating the ra6m5 wording would have introduced an error into the one file that did not have it — the mirror image of D128 §5's "citing a sibling without opening it", and the reason its comment now says *do not copy that sentence to ra6m5/ra8m2*.

5. Line citations are now machine-checked — scripts/check_arch_lines.py

Every one of the document's ~25 port citations went stale twice in one day, and neither time did any CMake change: once from the PXN correction in 2c6d4feb2 (D128), once from the comment pass in this entry. check_docs.py cannot see this — the file exists and the D-numbers resolve, so each reference stays "valid" while pointing at the wrong line. **A line number that drifts silently is worse than no line number**, because a reader who follows it finds a plausible neighbouring construct and believes it.

So the checker pairs each citation with a regex the cited line must match: 40 port lines and 15 upstream, 55 total, fail-on-stale with the correct line reported. It is not a generator — the numbers sit in prose that explains each block, so a human has to look. Hook step 2b runs it when BUILD_ARCHITECTURE.md or the table is staged.

It earned itself on the first run, catching an off-by-one in a correction this entry was making: :736 is the target_sources inside the accelerator block, :735 is the if().

Correction to D128

D128 pinned the document's header to TF-M 2c6d4feb2. That pin was stale the moment this entry's comment pass landed. Pinning a commit in prose has the same defect as the line numbers it was meant to qualify; the checker replaces it.

Method note

Three passes have now each found the same shape, one level further out. D126: check the explanation against the build files. D128: check the sibling entry you are citing. Here: check the comment you are quoting. The port comments were treated as a source throughout BUILD_ARCHITECTURE.md because they are detailed and confident, and four of them were years out of date. A comment is evidence of what someone believed when they wrote it — the same thing this log says about its own superseded entries, and it deserves the same scepticism.

D130 — TF-M 2.3 is deferred, not cancelled: the gate is FSP's Mbed TLS 4.1 migration, expected ~2026-11-12

Date: 2026-10-22 · Status: Accepted · Supersedes: D035 · Evidence: decision from the rm_psa_crypto owner; closes the D035/PROJECT_PLAN.md contradiction raised by the v3 review (F087 thread)

Decision. TF-M 2.3 / TF-PSA-Crypto is deferred, gated on FSP completing its **Mbed TLS v4.1 migration** — expected within three weeks of this entry, so ~2026-11-12. D035 said the rebase was cancelled; that is superseded. The port stays on v2.2.0 / Mbed TLS 3.6.3 until the gate clears, which is the same working state either word implies — but the planning consequence is opposite, and PROJECT_PLAN.md has been asserting "future work" against an Accepted entry that said "cancelled" since 2026-09-21.

Why a dependency and not a date. Mbed TLS 4.x is where the crypto library splits out as TF-PSA-Crypto, and that split is precisely what TF-M 2.3 consumes: 2.3.0 pins TF-PSA-Crypto v1.1.0, 2.3.1 pins v1.1.1 (D035). Rebasing before FSP has migrated would mean carrying FSP's 3.6-era crypto stack onto a TF-M that cannot host it — the *_ALT mechanism the port's SCE9 acceleration is built on does not exist above 3.6. So the gate is FSP's migration landing, not a calendar slot. Re-confirm the version pairing when it does; "4.1" and "TF-PSA-Crypto 1.1.1" are stated here as given, not as verified against a released manifest.

What survives from D035. Its body stays the reference for the rebase itself and nothing in it is withdrawn:

  • the four-item upstream delta (items 9 and 11 fixed upstream, 10 obsolete, 6 still needed at the relocated bl2/ext/mcuboot/scripts/wrapper.py);
  • the SPM-logging rewrite (lib/tfm_log, ERROR_RAW/INFO_RAW), which removes SPMLOG_*, tfm_spm_log.h and the TFM_SPM_LOG_LEVEL_SILENCE vocabulary — so item 7 and the RTT SPM-log backend both need porting, and CONFIG_TFM_BACKTRACE_ON_CORE_PANIC (GCC-only) overlaps item 7;
  • 10 of 20 surviving shared files conflicted.

One stale reference inside D035. It says "P5 of PROJECT_PLAN.md is cancelled". That is the plan numbering as of 2026-09-21; the plan was renumbered when RA8x2 became the primary goal, and this work is now P7. Today's P5 is RA8x2 single-core, which is done. Anyone reading D035 against the current plan would cancel the wrong phase — the hazard D128 rule 7 exists for, except here it is prose, so it stays and this entry is the correction.

Consequences that do not change. The "TF-M 2.3 debt grows while deferred" risk row stands and is now correctly worded: every change to a shared file adds to the eventual P7 rebase, and upstream submission of the port waits on it. The ALT route remains Mbed TLS 3.6-only and is redone as a PSA transparent driver in P7, following the rsip7 CM driver model. The TF-PSA-Crypto work itself lives in the sibling fsp_tf_psa_crypto repository with its own decision log (GETTING_STARTED.md), not here.

D131 — the v5 review: two generators were passing against their own faulty output; the RA6M5 PXN correction gets the entry it never had

Date: 2026-10-22 · Status: Accepted · Corrects: D047, D128, D129, D130 · Evidence: v5 findings F001, F283, F309, F313–F334; both tool fixes tested against induced failures

The fifth review found no open high-severity items but reported that the previous round introduced two tool defects. Both let errors pass the repository's own checks. Those are recorded first because they determine how much the other checks are worth.

1. The glossary dropped every correction (F309)

build_settled.py gained a sixth Standing column, Closed by, in D128. build_course_glossary.py read the last cell of each row. The last cell became Closed by, which is — for 127 of 130 entries, so every correction vanished. All 42 cited entries read a bare "stands". D113 should read "corrected by D117, D120, D126".

--check passed throughout, because it compares the generator's output with the page that generator last wrote. A parser reading the wrong column agrees with itself.

Two changes. The parser now reads SETTLED.md by column name and raises if the column is absent, so a renamed or reordered column stops the build instead of producing a wrong page. A second guard counts Corrects: fields in DECISIONS.md and fails if the log records corrections that the table does not show. It reports the counts either way, per D121.

The guard fired on its first run and named D090 and D098. Both were false positives: each is superseded and corrected by the same entry, where D128 drops the redundant "also corrected by" on purpose. The guard now checks standing rows only.

2. check_arch_lines.py did not run when TF-M changed (F321)

The checker exists to catch line drift caused by a TF-M comment edit. A TF-M commit does not run this repository's hook, so the check fired only at the next fsp_cmake commit that staged BUILD_ARCHITECTURE.md. D129 §5 stated the trigger as though it covered the cause.

scripts/pre-commit-tfm now runs the same check from the TF-M clone, on any staged platform/ext/target/renesas/ file. install_hooks.sh installs it. Tested by inserting one comment line into ra6m5/CMakeLists.txt: the hook reported 28 of 55 citations stale, named the correct line for each, and blocked the commit.

3. Corrections to D129

ClaimCorrect

The citation table now holds 39 port, 29 upstream and 4 local rows, 72 in total. F320 found about 15 cited lines with no row at all. That gap was not theoretical: writing the BRIDGING_FILES.md fix in this same pass, I cited ra8m2's FSP_EXCLUDED_MODULES at :159 when it is at :112, and nothing objected.

4. The RA6M5 PXN correction, recorded here (F332)

2c6d4feb2 corrected a claim that had no entry. The ra6m5 PXN comment said a TFM_PXN_ENABLE=ON configure of that platform "passes the armv8.1-m.main gate". It cannot. config/check_config.cmake:91 rejects TFM_PXN_ENABLE unless TFM_SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE is armv8.1-m.main, and ra6m5/cpuarch.cmake:15 sets armv8-m.main. PXN is an Armv8.1-M feature and the Cortex-M33 does not implement it, so the configure fails by design.

The paragraph was copied from ra8m2, where the measurement was taken and is valid (cpuarch.cmake:24). The commit cited D128 for this, which was wrong; it belongs here. What holds for RA6M5 is narrower: the define is plumbed PUBLIC on platform_s and would reach the HAL through tfm_spm if the part could use the feature.

5. Three mechanisms, not one — extends D129 §1 (F313, F314)

D129 established that the sce module builds r_sce. It did not name the mechanism that does exclude sources, so BRIDGING_FILES.md and ADDING_FSP_MODULES.md kept describing FSP_MODULES_NEVER_BUILT as an exclusion list.

MechanismWhereEffect
FSP_MODULES_S / _BL2ra6m5/CMakeLists.txt:234, :238the only thing that builds FSP sources for the secure and BL2 images
FSP_MODULES_NEVER_BUILT:266suppresses the unclaimed-directory warning; excludes no source
FSP_EXCLUDED_MODULES:112, used by fsp_collect_sources() at :1023filters sources out of the non-secure glob only

r_sce is in FSP_MODULES_NEVER_BUILT and built by the sce module and excluded from the NS glob. All three are true, for different roles.

A related claim in BRIDGING_FILES.md §3 was also wrong, and it affected a check for a silent failure. The section said FSP's flash_map_backend.h "reaches no include path". fsp_bsp.cmake:106-108 puts FSP's mcu-tools MCUboot headers on the BSP library's include path, because the bootloader project's hal_data.h includes rm_mcuboot_port.h. Those paths are PRIVATE to fsp_bsp_bl2 and never reach bootutil, which is what makes the arrangement safe. **An fsp_bsp object therefore reports a 12-byte struct flash_area legitimately, and the DWARF check has to be scoped to bootutil objects** or it reports a false failure on the one surface where nothing else in the build would.

6. Smaller corrections

  • D130 named the wrong Mbed TLS version (F333). 3.6.3 is TF-M's bundled copy, which the crypto partition has not used since D042. The port builds crypto from FSP's Mbed TLS, recorded as 3.6.6 in D047.
  • D035 still read Accepted (F334). Rule 2 requires the superseded entry to carry the line, and rule 7 permits the repair. Set to Superseded by D130. SETTLED.md was correct only because it derives the relation from D130's field.
  • bl2_boot_hal.c is not gated the same way on both parts (F316). On ra6m5 it is under if(CRYPTO_HW_ACCELERATOR). On ra8m2 it is unconditional, because it enables the SAU and BL2 cannot read the non-secure slots without it; only ra_sce_init.c is gated there.
  • RA6E1_SOLUTION.md claimed FSP 6.7.0-beta0 (F283). RA6E1 is dormant and its projects are on 6.6.0-rc1. Only RA6M5 and RA8M2 were uprevved.
  • D130 and PROJECT_PLAN.md gave P7 two different gates (F328). The Mbed TLS v4.1 migration is the gate. The rsip7 update supplies the driver model.

Process note

docs/STYLE_EDIT_PROMPT.md became a standing instruction during this pass. This entry is written to it: short declarative sentences, one claim each, and emphasis only on the one hazard in §5. Earlier entries are not rewritten, because rule 1 forbids it, but the style applies from here.

The pattern across four reviews now reads: check the explanation against the build files (D126), check the sibling entry you cite (D128), check the comment you quote (D129), and check that your checker can fail. Both defects in §1 and §2 were tools that reported success without testing anything — one compared a generator with itself, the other never ran on the commits that cause the drift it detects.

D132 — the RA6M4 brick is a write to a reserved area; no field needs naming

Date: 2026-10-22 · Status: Superseded by D133 · Corrects: D094, D065, D120 · Evidence: the RA6M4 hardware manual's option-setting memory map, and the owner's reading of it

The gaps between the option-setting groups are reserved. The hardware manual requires that reserved areas are not written at all. A coalesced PT_LOAD writes zeros across them, and that write bricks the part.

That is the whole cause. D094 went looking for the individual field that died, disproved two candidates (FSPR permanence, which RA6M4 does not implement, and OFS1_SEL content, which was byte-identical to a working board) and left the question open. The question does not need an answer: writing a reserved area is itself the fault, whatever a particular reserved word happens to control on a particular part.

What this changes in the record. The measurement in D094 stands unaltered: the preserved image emitted three OFS words and ld produced one PT_LOAD of 388 bytes (0x184) spanning 0x0100A100-0x0100A283, of which 376 bytes were zero fill. What is withdrawn is the framing around it — "which field dies is unknown", "treat PBPS as the surviving candidate", and the suggestion that the cause remained open. D065's PBPS attribution is not revived either; PBPS is one reserved word among the many the fill covers.

What this changes in the documents. Every statement of the form "the mechanism is proven but the field responsible is unknown" is replaced by "the fill writes reserved areas, which the hardware manual forbids". The hazard statements themselves are untouched: one MEMORY region per group, check_ofs.py on every BL2, flash .elf/.hex and never .bin.

Why the hedge was there. The port reconstructed the cause from a dead board and the image that killed it, and treated the hardware manual's reserved-area rule as background rather than as the answer. A rule in the manual outranks an inference from two boards.

D133 — the coalesced fill zeroes eight DEFINED option registers, not only reserved bytes; D132 overstated the reserved-area reading

Date: 2026-10-22 · Status: Accepted · Supersedes: D132 · Corrects: D132 · Evidence: bringup/bricking_evidence/bl2_BRICKED.elf program headers and segment contents crossed against ra6m4/region_defs.h's thirteen OPTION_SETTING_* groups; the v6 review's F346, re-verified here rather than taken on report

D132 said the fill covered reserved bytes and that "PBPS is one reserved word among the many the fill covers". Both halves are wrong. PBPS is a defined one-time register, and the fill reaches eight defined registers as well as the reserved bytes between them.

Measured. The preserved image carries one R PT_LOAD at 0x0100A100, FileSiz 0x184 (388 bytes), holding .option_setting_ofs0, .option_setting_ofs1_sec and .option_setting_ofs1_sel. Dumping those 388 bytes gives 0x00 everywhere except three words:

addressvaluegroup
0x0100A100ffffffffOFS0, emitted
0x0100A200fffdffffOFS1_SEC, emitted
0x0100A280f8f8ffffOFS1_SEL, emitted

Crossing the span 0x0100A100-0x0100A283 against the part's option map, eight defined groups lie inside it and were written 0x00:

groupaddresslength
DUALSEL0x0100A1100x4
OFS10x0100A1800x4
BANKSEL0x0100A1900x4
BPS0x0100A1C00xC
PBPS0x0100A1E00xC
BANKSEL_SEC0x0100A2100x4
BPS_SEC0x0100A2400xC
PBPS_SEC0x0100A2600xC

BANKSEL_SEL (0x0100A290) and BPS_SEL (0x0100A2C0) sit above the segment and were untouched.

So the cause is a write the image never intended, to registers it never declared. Two of the eight are the one-time Permanent Block Protect pair. Writing zeros to a reserved area is forbidden by the hardware manual and remains a fault in its own right, which is what D132 recorded correctly; what it got wrong was that the fill hits nothing else. It hits eight named registers, and PBPS = 0 is a documented permanent effect.

Which field killed the boards is still not established. That is D094's position and this entry returns to it. D065 named PBPS; the dump shows PBPS was indeed zeroed, so D065 is a live candidate again rather than a withdrawn one, but a candidate is not a finding: seven other defined registers took the same write, and the part never came back to be asked. Do not state a single field as the cause in any document.

Not verified here. The RA6M4 hardware manual is not in either tree, so this entry does not assert what the manual says about reserved areas beyond the owner's statement that they must not be written, and it does not assert what PBPS = 0 does to a part beyond FSP's naming of it as permanent.

The hazard rules are unchanged, and were unchanged by D132 too. One linker MEMORY region per option group; check_ofs.py after every BL2 link; readelf -l as the only place the coalescing shows; flash .elf or .hex and never the flat .bin.

Process note. D132 was written from a one-line statement about reserved areas and was not checked against the preserved image, which is in this repository and takes two commands to read. The entry then propagated into six documents and three port comments before anything tested it. The rule the log already had — check the explanation against the artifact (D126), and check that your checker can fail (D131) — applies to a decision entry as much as to a tool.

D134 — the 2026-10-23 technical review: the five high findings hold against source

Date: 2026-10-23 · Status: Accepted · Evidence: docs/General_tech_review/PORT_TECHNICAL_REVIEW.md and port_review_findings.csv at TF-M a18fd18c8 / fsp_cmake f30860e; every claim below re-read in the tree rather than taken on report (D133 process note)

Six tracks produced 167 findings, consolidated to 5 high, 36 medium, 53 low and 49 info, with no critical finding and no NS-to-S memory-isolation bypass in the shipped configuration. This entry records what was verified. D135 records what was changed.

P01 — development keys and dummy provisioning are the shipped default. Verified. MCUBOOT_HW_KEY OFF (ra6m5/config.cmake:99, ra8m2/config.cmake:107); PLATFORM_DEFAULT_{NV_COUNTERS,CRYPTO_KEYS,OTP,PROVISIONING} ON (ra6m5:200-203, ra8m2:226-229); TFM_DUMMY_PROVISIONING overridden by neither part, so it keeps the config/config_base.cmake:132 default of ON; MCUBOOT_KEY_S/NS overridden by neither part, so they keep the in-tree root-EC-P256*.pem of mcuboot_default_config.cmake:63-64. The only key-related override either part makes is MCUBOOT_SIGNATURE_TYPE "EC-P256" (ra6m5:68, ra8m2:75). With HW_KEY OFF the trust anchor is the key arrays in bl2/ext/mcuboot/keys.c, so changing MCUBOOT_KEY_S/NS alone re-signs the images and leaves BL2 trusting the sample keys.

P02 — anti-rollback is inert. Verified. MCUBOOT_HW_ROLLBACK_PROT ON (mcuboot_default_config.cmake:45) with MCUBOOT_SECURITY_COUNTER_S/NS fixed at 1 (:74-75) and no override in either part. MCUBOOT_DOWNGRADE_PREVENTION appears nowhere under bl2/.

**P03 — the clock, wait-state and operating-mode SARs are non-secure writable. Verified, and fixable from the port without a generator fix.** All four secure projects generate BSP_CFG_CLOCKS_SECURE (0) (ra_gen/bsp_clock_cfg.h in ra6m5_{gcc,iar}_secure and ra8m2_{gcc,iar}_CPU0_secure), so R_BSP_SecurityInit writes the non-secure-open arm of each #if BSP_CFG_CLOCKS_SECURE branch:

partregistersecure valuevalue in force
RA6M5CGFSAR0xFFE0E4020xFFFFFFFF
RA6M5FSAR0xFEFE0xFFFF
RA6M5SRAMSARbit 1 clearbit 1 set
RA8M2CGFSAR0x00x1F7F7FFD
RA8M2LPMSARbit 0 clearbit 0 set
RA8M2MSAR00, already overridden

Each of these is #ifndef-guarded in the generated bsp_mcu_family_cfg.h, so the port can supply it from FSP_COMPILE_DEFS exactly as it already does for BSP_TZ_CFG_MSAR=0 (ra8m2/CMakeLists.txt:227). The generator defect D093 records blocks BSP_CFG_CLOCKS_SECURE (1), not the individual overrides. Do not reach for -DBSP_CFG_CLOCKS_SECURE=1: bsp_clock_cfg.h defines it unguarded, and on BL2 it also selects the TrustZone arm of the OFS1_SEL formula (ra6m5/CMakeLists.txt:186-206).

**P04 — secure debug and the DLM lifecycle are neither enforced nor reflected. Verified at code level.** init_debug() returns TFM_PLAT_ERR_SUCCESS at ra6m5/target_cfg.c:138-141 and in the ra8m2 equivalent, and has no caller in either port: every init_debug() call site in the tree is an arm/ platform. The reported lifecycle comes from map_otp_lcs_to_tfm_slc() alone. The DLM register semantics are the review's architecture knowledge, not a manual, and the manual is in neither tree.

P05 — an open multi-part operation blocks the TRNG. Verified at code level, not run. 44 SCE9 primitives under ra6m5_gcc_secure/.../sce9/plainkey/primitive/ open with if (RD1_MASK(REG_1BCH, 0x0000001fU) != 0) return FSP_ERR_CRYPTO_SCE_RESOURCE_CONFLICT;, and HW_SCE_GenerateRandomNumberSub is one of them (hw_sce_p_p20.c:12-14, exactly as cited). The port turns that refusal into PSA_ERROR_HARDWARE_FAILURE rather than a busy or retry status (ra6m5/sce_trng.c:73), after zeroising the buffer. One step is inference, not verification: the review describes hw_sce_p_p47i.c:15-17 as taking the lock, where those three lines test it and return RESOURCE_CONFLICT. Whether the Init call leaves REG_1BCH set is inside the obfuscated WR1_PROG sequence and was not read.

Where the review states a mechanism loosely.

  • R095 says the guard "never inspects bl2.elf". The guard inspects $<TARGET_FILE:bl2>, which is bl2.axf; bl2.elf is objcopy -O elf32-littlearm of that same file (toolchain_GNUARM.cmake:283-291), so the verdict carries over in practice. The gap R095 and R096 share is real and lies elsewhere: the guard and strip targets are ALL targets, so a build that is not ALL runs neither.
  • P03 recommends a build-time #error while the generated value is 0. Not adopted: in the present state that fails every build.

What the review did not cover, in its own words. No builds and no hardware runs; the only binaries were RA6M5 ELFs from 2026-09-23, a month older than the source; no RA8M2 build outputs exist; no RA hardware manuals, so SAR, DLM, MRAM-programming and data-flash erased-value semantics come from FSP sources; all test statuses come from this file. The ten uncommitted working-tree entries it declined to inspect were the untracked docs/artifacts* review directories, START_REVIEW.md and one .jlink file, with no port source among them.

D135 — eight defects from the 2026-10-23 review are fixed now; P01-P05 and the brick-path restructure are the owner's

Date: 2026-10-23 · Status: Accepted · Evidence: D134; the commits named below

The review's five high findings are configuration policy, a hardening change that removes non-secure access, or unobserved runtime behaviour. None is a defect a reader of the tree can settle, so this round takes what is mechanical and leaves the rest stated.

Fixed.

findingchange
R156check_ofs.py tool errors exit 2 through a die() helper. Exit 1 is the DO-NOT-FLASH verdict, and a missing readelf was returning it.
R155RA6M5's BPS and PBPS words are 0x10 (ra6m5/region_defs.h:297,299) and ra6m5_bl2.ld gives each its own 0x10 region, so --max-word 0xC would have failed the build on a legitimately placed BPS group. Raised to 0x10 at both call sites; 0xC is right for RA6E1 and RA6M4. The guard loses nothing: the closest two words on this map are OFS0 (0x0100A100+4) and DUALSEL (0x0100A110), so the smallest coalescable span is 0x14.
-check_ofs.py still attributed the brick to "block-protect programmed to 0" and called it permanent, in two printed messages. D133 withdrew both. The 2026-10-22 sweep missed them.
R148ra8m2/bl2_boot_hal.c writes ns_end - 1 to SAU->RLAR. RLAR.LADDR is the inclusive limit of the 32-byte block it names, so FSP's ns_end ran BL2's one SAU region 32 bytes past the end of MRAM. This is a deliberate deviation from the FSP expression that block is otherwise a verbatim copy of, and the same off-by-one belongs in a report to FSP.
R130cmsis_override.h defines CMSE_NONSECURE as 18, the ACLE value, not 1. Latent either way: both RA6M5 binaries use 18, because arm_cmse.h redefines the macro after the pre-include.
R020The RA8M2 isolation-3 comment justified PXN being off with "needs armv8.1-m.main". ra8m2/cpuarch.cmake:24 sets armv8.1-m.main, so PXN is available on this part and is simply not enabled.
R160The BL2_HALT_AT_MAIN guard in the shared bl2/ext/mcuboot/bl2_main.c named -DRA6M4_BL2_HALT_AT_MAIN, the RA6M4 FAWMON address 0x407FE0DC, a bit-15 liveness reading and a permanent brick. The option is <PART>_BL2_HALT_AT_MAIN, the RA6M4 has no Flash Access Window, and D133 withdrew the permanence.
R112tfm_config.log, a 312-line failed ra6m4 configure log at the TF-M repository root, is deleted. UPSTREAM_CHANGES.md had already called it an accident that should be deleted; its file count goes from 39 to 38 and the unaccounted-for count from 19 to 18.

Every edit to a file cited by line is word-level with the line count unchanged, so no citation moved. ra8m2/bl2_boot_hal.c:91-95, bl2_main.c:112-125 and ra8m2/config.cmake:225 are all cited, and all three files are the length they were.

Left for the owner, with the reason.

findingwhy it is not taken here
P01, P02Product decisions: real keys, a provisioning flow, release-managed counters and a downgrade-rejected test. Both are inherited upstream development defaults, so a production profile is new port surface rather than a correction.
P03Implementable today from FSP_COMPILE_DEFS, and D134 names each register and value. It takes clock, wait-state and low-power register access away from the non-secure world, so it needs a hardware run on both parts and both toolchains, not a source edit.
P04Needs the DLM register map, which is in neither tree.
P05FSP engine-lock lifetime, inside rm_psa_crypto territory, and never observed running.
R096, R095The brick-path closure is structural and the choice matters. Three routes: rename the unsafe output inside the generic add_convert_to_bin_target, which touches every platform; give the platform its own flat-binary rule for bl2; or delete the flashable artefacts when the guard fails. Recommended: the third, with the guard as a dependency, because it is the only one that also covers the .elf, .hex and .srec that a failed guard leaves in bin/ today.
R142FSP r_mram.c 32-byte crossing, unconfirmed on hardware, and FSP's to fix.
P08 and the matrixHardware.

Process note. The five highs were verified before any of them was acted on, which is what D133 asked for after D132 was written from a report. One of the eight fixes above is the 2026-10-22 sweep's own residue in check_ofs.py, found by reading the file rather than by a checker: no checker in this repository reads the port's printed output.
